stories.title: Ocean Pearl Apartments Inaugurated in Perseverance (Seychelles)
stories.description: The inauguration of Ocean Pearl Apartments in Perseverance (Seychelles) was presided over by the Seychelles president (Patrick Herminie); 24 three-bedroom units were handed over to families from the housing and landbank lists. The project is valued at SCR 27,700,620.64, including SCR 24,175,081.50 for construction and SCR 3,525,539.14 for external works and supporting infrastructure; the government covers the latter costs, described as approximately 13% of the total. The publication dated 6 October 2026 reports the inauguration; the event date is not specified.

publications.text:
24 families receive keys to Ocean Pearl Apartments 

by T. Dennis 

Twenty-four families received the keys to their new homes at the newly inaugurated Ocean Pearl Apartments at Ile Perseverance yesterday, as President Patrick Herminie revealed that more than 3,000 families remain on the housing assistance waiting list. The three-block development was inaugurated as part of the launch of Habitat Week, being observed under the theme ‘Adequate Housing for All’. Each block comprises eight three-bedroom units, bringing the total to 24 homes.

For full context and detailed reporting, read the complete article in today’s edition. Subscribe by calling +248 4290999 or email us at sales@today.sc

“Housing Is More Than Four Walls and a Roof. It Is Dignity, Security and Family”

24 Mid-Range Condominium Units Inaugurated to Launch Habitat Week

The inauguration ceremony was presided over by the President of the Republic, Dr Patrick Herminie, who was accompanied by First Lady Veronique Herminie, Vice President Sébastien Pillay, Cabinet of Ministers and Leader of Government Business, Hon. Sylvanne Lemiel. Also present were Principal Secretaries from various Ministries that contributed to the project, staff of the Ministry of Lands and Housing, and other partners and stakeholders.

The name “Ocean Pearl Apartments”, was chosen by the future homeowners themselves and inspired by the development’s beautiful setting. The 24 three-bedroom units were handed over to families who had been waiting patiently on the housing and landbank lists, many of whom had faced social and economic challenges in their pursuit of homeownership.

The project is valued at SCR 27,700,620.64, comprising SCR 24,175,081.50 for the construction of the 24 residential units and SCR 3,525,539.14 for external works and supporting infrastructure.

Under the mid-range condominium arrangement, the cost of the residential units is borne by the new homeowners, while the Government covers the cost of the external works and supporting infrastructure. This represents a Government subsidy of approximately 13 percent of the total project cost.

Read full article: https://statehouse.gov.sc/news/7285/housing-is-more-than-four-walls-and-a-roof-it-is-dignity-security-and-family?

stories.title: Coast Guard Maritime Incident Inquiry Board Takes Oath
stories.description: The board established to investigate a maritime incident involving Seychelles Coast Guard officers took its oath of office on 12 October 2026. Justice Antony Fernando was sworn in as chairperson, with Captain Robert Marie and Ronny Matatiken as commissioners; Dr Simon Mutungi will serve as secretary.

publications.text:
Three members of the Board of Inquiry established to investigate the maritime incident involving Seychelles Coast Guard officers took their oath of office this morning at a ceremony held in the presence of the President of the Republic, Dr Patrick Herminie; Vice-President Mr Sébastien Pillay; Chief of Staff, Ms Jenifer Vel; and Chief of Defence Forces Major General Michael Rosette

Justice Antony Fernando took the oath of office as Chairperson, alongside Captain Robert Marie and Mr Ronny Matatiken, who were sworn in as Commissioners.

Dr Simon Mutungi will serve as Secretary to the Board.

Read more: https://statehouse.gov.sc/news/7295/defence-board-of-inquiry-into-maritime-incident-takes-oath-of-office

The swearing-in of a Board of Inquiry into an incident involving a Seychelles Coast Guard vessel and its crew at sea on September 16, 2026, took place this morning at State House.

The three-member board is chaired by Justice Anthony Fernando. The other two members are seasoned pilot, Captain Robert Marie and Ronny Matatiken who specializes in maritime security and operations. The board’s secretary is Ugandan national, Dr Simon Mutungi.

(Video Credit: State House)

stories.title: 104.7 Kilograms of Waste Removed from Anse Forbans (Seychelles) Marsh
stories.description: On 7 November 2026, IOTA Seychelles organised a clean-up of the Anse Forbans (Seychelles) marsh, where nine volunteers collected 104.7 kg of waste in one morning. Coco Farm says it supported the initiative.

publications.text:
This morning team members from the Indian Ocean Tortoise Alliance(IOTA), the Founder of Coco Farm and 9 young volunteers took to the wetlands within Anse Marie-Louise area near Anse Forbans beach to help clean up the space🦀

By the end of the clean-up activity, the team successfully collected 104.7 KG of Litter

By:H.Siu

IOTA marsh clean-up removes over 104kg of waste 

by H. Siu 

Volunteers collected 104.7 kilograms of litter from the Anse Marie-Louise wetland, near Anse Forbans Beach, on Saturday, 7 November, during a community clean-up organised by the Indian Ocean Tortoise Alliance (IOTA) in collaboration with Coco Farm. The activity brought together IOTA representatives, Coco Farm founder Jean-Christian Pillay and six young volunteers, who joined efforts to remove waste from the marshland as part of the organisation’s ongoing ‘Adopt a Marsh’ initiative.

For full context and detailed reporting, read the complete article in today’s edition. Subscribe by calling +248 4290999 or email us at sales@today.sc

Our little corner of Seychelles deserves our care.

Anse Forbans is not only where Coco Farm calls home. It is also home to a beautiful marsh ecosystem and the wildlife that depends on it.

Last Saturday, IOTA Seychelles organised a clean-up of the Anse Forbans marsh. Nine volunteers came together and collected an amazing 104.7 kg of waste in just one morning.

Coco Farm was proud to support this initiative and to play a small part in helping keep our local environment clean and healthy.

We sincerely thank IOTA Seychelles and all the volunteers who showed up and did the hard work. 💚

Supporting our community and protecting the environment around us will always be part of what Coco Farm stands for.

Let’s keep looking after the places we call home.

stories.title: Seychelles Reaffirms 30% Nature Protection Commitment
stories.description: A Twitter publication dated 4 November 2026 reports that Minister Barry Faure reaffirmed Seychelles’ commitment to the Commonwealth Nature Initiative during a meeting with Senator Russ Feingold. The commitment supports global efforts to protect 30% of land and oceans by 2030; the meeting’s date and location are not specified.

publications.text:
Minister Barry Faure reaffirmed Seychelles’ commitment to the Commonwealth Nature Initiative, supporting global efforts to protect 30% of land and oceans by 2030 in meeting with Senator Russ Feingold.

Follow the below link to read more:
https://t.co/LoK5LGWUFA https://t.co/pH8zFVd8vG

Meeting between Minister Barry Faure and Senator Russ Feingold, Chair of the Global Steering Committee of the Campaign for Nature

The Minister for Foreign Affairs and the Diaspora, Mr. Barry Faure, met with Senator Russ Feingold, Chair of the Global Steering Committee of the Campaign for Nature, on the sidelines of CHOGM 2026, in St Johns.

During the meeting, Senator Feingold expressed his appreciation to Seychelles for its support towards the launch of the Commonwealth Nature Initiative (CNI), held on 2 November 2026 in St. John’s, Antigua and Barbuda.

The four-year initiative seeks to accelerate land and ocean conservation efforts across the Commonwealth, mobilising governments, philanthropic organisations and the private sector to invest in national and regional programmes that support the achievement of the global 30x30 target - protecting and conserving at least 30 per cent of the world’s land and oceans by 2030 - with a particular focus on low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries.

Follow the below link to read more:
https://mfa.gov.sc/news/meeting-between-minister-barry-faure-and-senator-russ-feingold-chair-of-the-global-steering-committee-of-the-campaign-for-nature/

stories.title: Seychelles Police Academy Resumes Recruiting S5 Graduates
stories.description: In an interview published on 9 October 2026, Academy Commandant Assistant Superintendent Hendrika Marie said the Seychelles Police Academy had resumed recruiting candidates who completed S5. She said trainees cover 17 modules and that 35 of the 56 candidates in the intake graduated; newly trained officers are expected to be deployed to police stations according to operational needs.

publications.text:
Thirty Five Trainee Constables took their oath this afternoon during a passing out ceremony held at the Seychelles Police Academy, marking the successful completion of their training and the beginning of their journey as new trainee in the Seychelles Police Force.

The ceremony was held in the presence of His Excellency Dr Patrick Herminie, President of the Republic of Seychelles; Minister for Homeland Security and Civil Affairs Mr James Camille; Major General Michael Rosette; Commissioner of Police, Mr Godfra Hermitte; Deputy Commissioners of Police Mr Ned Wirtz and Dr Jemmy Bouzin; senior police officers, family members and other invited guests.

The newly graduated officers successfully completed an intensive 18 month training programme covering 17 modules, equipping them with the knowledge, skills and discipline required to serve and protect the people of Seychelles.

56 recruits initially joined the Academy after completing their secondary education. Today, 35 have successfully completed the programme, demonstrating the commitment, perseverance and determination required to overcome the challenges of police training and pursue a career in law enforcement.

Beyond the celebrations, the occasion carried a deeply emotional significance for six of the graduating officers who experienced the heartbreaking loss of a parent during their training. Among them was one officer who lost both her mother and father.

Despite the pain of losing their loved ones, these sixth officers found the strength to persevere and fulfil their dream of graduating from the Academy. Their achievement stands as a powerful testament to resilience, courage and the determination to keep moving forward, even in life's most difficult moments.

As a gesture of compassion, respect and solidarity, the Commandant of the Seychelles Police Academy, Assistant Superintendent Hendrika Marie, presented the four officers with bouquets of flowers. Although their parents were not physically present to witness this important milestone, their love, memories and influence will forever remain part of their journey. One can only imagine the pride and happiness their parents would have felt seeing them take this significant step towards a future of service and dedication.

Today, as these four officers join the Seychelles Police Force, they do not stand alone. They become part of a new family the family in blue where their colleagues stand beside them, sharing in their triumphs, supporting them through life's challenges and honouring the memories of those they have lost.

In an interview with the press, the Commandant of the Seychelles Police Academy  Assistant Superintendent Hendrika Marie explained that the Academy has resumed recruiting candidates who have completed their S5 studies. She noted that experience has shown that younger recruits are generally easier to mould, discipline and guide throughout their training. At this stage of their lives, they are often more determined and motivated to succeed, with the aim of completing their training and graduating at the age of 18.

The Commandant explained that the trainees covered 17 modules across various fields, including policing, law, academy studies, human rights and anatomy. Upon graduation, the newly trained officers are expected to be deployed across various police stations, depending on the operational needs and demands of the Seychelles Police Force.

She also highlighted that the selection process maintains a balance between male and female candidates. However, she observed that female recruits have demonstrated strong persistence and determination throughout the training, contributing to the increasing number of female graduates.

Addressing the number of trainees who completed the programme, the Commandant stated that out of the 56 candidates who initially joined the intake, 35 successfully graduated. She clarified that those who left the Academy did not necessarily depart because of disciplinary issues, but rather because some realised that policing and the demands of Academy life were not suited to them.

stories.title: Seychelles Firefighters Complete Shipboard Firefighting Training
stories.description: From 28 September to 16 October 2026, two instructors from Marseille (France)’s naval fire battalion trained firefighters from the Seychelles Fire and Rescue Services Agency in responding to fires aboard ships. The three-week programme included theory, practical exercises aboard docked vessels, and training future trainers to support continued skills transfer.

publications.text:
🚒🚢 La coopération franco-seychelloise au service de la sécurité maritime !

Pendant trois semaines, du 28 septembre au 16 octobre 2026, deux instructeurs du Bataillon de marins-pompiers de Marseille (BMPM) ont partagé leur expertise avec les pompiers seychellois de la Seychelles Fire and Rescue Services Agency (SFRSA).

🎯 L’objectif ? Renforcer les capacités d’intervention des équipes seychelloises dans la lutte contre les incendies à bord des navires.

Au programme : enseignements théoriques, exercices pratiques à bord de navires à quai et partage d’expérience pour améliorer la sécurité et la coordination des interventions.

🤝 Une attention particulière a été portée à la formation de futurs formateurs, afin d’assurer une transmission durable des compétences.

👏 Bravo à tous les participants et merci aux formateurs et partenaires pour leur engagement !

#LaFranceAuxSeychelles #CoopérationFrancoSeychelloise #SécuritéMaritime #MarinsPompiers

Certificate Presentation Ceremony – Ship Fire Fighting Training

The successful completion of Ship Fire Fighting Training Levels 1 and 2 marks an important achievement in strengthening Seychelles’ maritime emergency preparedness and capacity to respond effectively to shipboard fire incidents.

To commemorate this achievement, the Seychelles Fire and Rescue Services Agency (SFRSA) held a certificate presentation ceremony to recognise the participants who completed the training, as well as the instructors whose expertise and commitment continue to enhance professional firefighting capabilities. The training was delivered by trainers from the French cooperation, with the support of the Government of France, and brought together representatives from the Seychelles Fire and Rescue Services Agency, the Seychelles Coast Guard, the Seychelles Ports Authority and the Seychelles Maritime Safety Agency.

The programme enhanced practical skills, operational readiness and inter-agency cooperation in managing shipboard fire emergencies.

The ceremony was attended by the Ambassador of France to Seychelles, Mrs Anne Talineau; the Principal Secretary for Homeland Security, Ms Michelle Sabury; the Chief Fire Officer, Ms Tally Domingue; and representatives of the participating organisations.

Congratulations to all participants on their achievement, and sincere thanks to the trainers from the French cooperation and all partners for their valuable contributions to this important training initiative.

publications.title: Press Conference on Adverse Weather Response and Rainy Season Preparedness
publications.text:
The government has intensified emergency response and coordination efforts following severe weather that brought heavy rainfall, flooding, fallen trees and landslides across Seychelles’ three main island regions. Authorities are warning that the recent weather could signal further challenges in November and December, traditionally among the wettest months of the year.

Speaking at a press conference yesterday, Vice-President Sebastien Pillay outlined the extent of the damage, ongoing emergency operations and rehabilitation efforts, as well as measures being taken to protect lives, homes and critical infrastructure.

According to the Vice-President, 736 emergency cases have been reported. Of these, 282 have been resolved, leaving 454 active cases. Ninety-two cases have been classified as high priority, while 27 families require immediate assistance or relocation.

Flooding and fallen trees account for the majority of incidents reported, while unstable slopes, large boulders and damaged road infrastructure continue to pose significant risks.

Mr Pillay said the government’s immediate priority is to protect lives and ensure interventions are effectively coordinated while gradually transitioning from emergency response to rehabilitation and long-term disaster-risk reduction.

​- La gestion des risques naturels face à la multiplication des événements climatiques extrêmes.  
​- La protection prioritaire des familles et des habitations touchées.
​- La remise en état rapide des infrastructures endommagées.

​La résilience de l'archipel et l'efficacité de la réponse publique face aux défis environnementaux restent plus que jamais au cœur des priorités.

stories.title: 116 Seychelles Citizenship Grants Went Undisclosed
stories.description: Minister for Homeland Security (James Camille) acknowledged that 116 foreign nationals were granted Seychelles citizenship during the United Seychelles administration’s first year without the publication required by the Citizenship Act. The matter came to light through a Private Notice Question by Opposition Leader (Bernard Georges) during 9–11 November 2026; 83 grants were under Section 5(1), 20 were through marriage and 13 through ancestry. The Opposition alleged disregard for statutory obligations and raised concerns about transparency and accountability.

publications.text:
Where are all those people who keep complaining about foreigners working in Seychelles? Read this 👇🏼

So what do you have to say about this? 116 people were granted Seychellois citizenship in 1 year, including 83 with no family ties to Seychelles, without their names being published in the Official Gazette as required by law.

🇸🇨 116 Seychellois passports in one year. Not one name made public.

In the National Assembly the Minister admitted it.
🔹 33 went to people who married a Seychellois or have a Seychellois parent.
🔹 83 went to people with no family link at all.

That is a lot of new citizens in just 12 months under President Herminie and Vice-President Pillay.

The law is clear. When someone becomes a citizen, their name, address and photo must be published in the Official Gazette within 30 days, so every Seychellois can see who is joining the nation.

The Minister confirmed it never happened.

Why hide the names?

Citizenship is not a private gift. A Seychellois passport is one of the strongest in Africa. It is our identity, our right to live here, our access to free health, education and land. Ordinary Seychellois work hard, pay taxes and struggle with the cost of living. Yet behind closed doors this privilege went to dozens of people with no blood or marriage connection to us, and the government refuses to tell us who they are.

People are already asking the obvious question. Were some of these 83 passports the price of campaign money?

We do not have the proof. But when a government breaks its own law on transparency, it invites that suspicion. If everything was clean, the names would already be in the Gazette.

Seychellois citizenship belongs to the people of this country.
❌ It is not for sale.
❌ It is not a reward handed out quietly.
❌ It is not something a government can hide from the citizens it serves.

The Assembly must now demand:
👉 the full list of names
👉 the reason each one was granted
👉 the missing Gazette publications

This is not a technical matter. It is about who we are as a nation, and whether those in power still respect the law and the people.

Share this. The people have a right to know. 🇸🇨

#Seychelles #SUM #SeychellesUnitedMovement #Citizenship #Transparency #RuleOfLaw #NationalAssembly

Today's presentation by Camille before the National Assembly (NA) , revealing that 116 foreigners, have received  Seychelois citizenship within just a year of this Mickey Mouse government being in office, raises serious questions,especially the 83 that received theirs under Section 5 '1'.

The most serious questions  that deserve the attention of every Seychelois are;
1. Is the United Seychelles (US) government turning the Seychelois citizenship into a commodity just like they did before?
2. Also is this banana government headed by Hermine and Pillay,developing a habit of handling our citizenship without sufficient transparency and accountability?
3. Is the citizenship and passport being offered to foreigners for as much as US$2 million each? If so, credited to whose Account?

Hermine and Pillay must know that governing a country comes with a responsibility, that is for protecting our sovereignty and nationality, also they have been entrusted with the obligation of safeguarding this country. They should not be  treating our nationality as something of their own, that they can distribute whenever they feel like it.

Furthermore, if citizenship is being granted through any investment or a citizenship programme, then this banana government must publish the applicable legal framework, financial requirements and approval procedures.

What is even more concerning are the allegations circulating  that some  of those individuals who received their citizenship by Hermine ,sponsored the US for the last election, thus  this is what they have been promised in return for their political and financial support. Additionally, if Hermine is the one who gives the final approval as stated by Camille, he must be accountable for the decision he signs off. We the people of Seychelles cannot allow the value of our nationality  to become a political convenience to Hermine and Pillay.

To conclude the Seychelles United Movement strongly believes that our citizenship laws must be respected, applied consistently and administered transparently, regardless of who is in power.
#seychelles #SeychellesUnitedMovement

I am shocked and deeply angered. As a Member of the National Assembly, I learned during this morning’s Private Notice Question that since assuming office in October 2025, President Patrick Herminie has granted Seychellois citizenship to 83 foreign nationals.

Who are these people? What nationalities did they originally hold? What extraordinary contributions have they made to qualify under Section 5(1) of the Citizenship Act? Why has this been kept secret from the Seychellois people?

Our citizenship is not a political gift. I demand a public inquiry to establish whether corruption, kickbacks or rewards linked to election sponsorship in 2025 played any part. Seychelles deserves answers!
 #StopAbuseOfPower #nocitizenshipforsale

Sesel an antye i dan sok pou tande ki zis dan en an ki kantite etranze k inn ganny nationalite seselwa anba sa prezidan soungoula lake kartron.Patrick patrick ou avek ou bann konplis pe fer avek nou pei en?inn ler pou nou bour ou deor.PATRICK OUT.

Bonzour tou seselwa ki sesel ou aletranze.
Sa ki mon pe al dir i mon lopinyon personnel.

Mon tya kontan ki dan sa pei in ler pou arete sa dil donn nou nasyonalite akoz nou pa don en permi pou reste pou lavi selman nou nasyonalite pa donnen selman swiv menm prosedir e fer li pli serye tou pou don sa permi reste pou lavi.Seselwa 83 pa enm pti limero avek nou grander popilasyon i en ta e fransman mon araze ler mon tand sa bann grenn lannen ale menm grenn.

In ler pou dir seselwa konbyen nasyonalite i annan epi pe donnen tou sa lannen i annan pou bez tonm sek ler zot pou tande.Mersi pas en bon lazournen.

116 New citizens, one big question: who broke the law? 

The United Seychelles administration has a rather uncomfortable problem: the Minister for Homeland Security has admitted that the law was not followed in granting citizenship to 116 foreign nationals during the Government’s first year in office.

Under the Citizenship Act, applications must be gazetted before approval, allowing the public an opportunity to comment. Approved applications must also be published within 30 days. The notices are required to include the applicant’s name, address and photograph.

None of the 116 cases was made public.

The matter only came to light this week through a Private Notice Question by Opposition Leader Bernard Georges in the National Assembly.

Minister James Camille dismissed the failure as an "omission". An interesting choice of words for what appears to be a wholesale failure to comply with the law.

The Opposition sees something far more serious: a blatant disregard for statutory obligations, a dangerous erosion of transparency and an environment in which abuse of presidential power and corruption can flourish without public scrutiny.

The numbers make the matter even more extraordinary.

Of the 116 new citizens:

20 were granted citizenship through marriage.

13 qualified through ancestry.

83 received citizenship under Section 5(1), which empowers the President to grant citizenship to individuals considered meritorious.

Eighty-three presidential discretionary grants in a single year. A remarkable figure by any measure.

There is no recent precedent for a Seychelles President exercising this particular power on such a scale in such a short period. Former President Wavel Ramkalawan did not use Section 5(1) during his entire presidency from 2020 to 2025.

The obvious questions are unavoidable.

Who are these 83 individuals? What have they contributed to Seychelles? Why was the legally required public disclosure ignored? And who is accountable for allowing this to happen?

Citizenship is not a presidential gift to be distributed behind closed doors. It is one of the most important privileges a country can confer on a foreign national.

If the law requires transparency, the President is not above that requirement.

And if 116 citizenship grants can pass through the highest office in the land without the legally required public scrutiny, Seychellois have every reason to ask what else is being decided behind closed doors.

A government that asks citizens to respect the law must first demonstrate that it respects the law itself.

Minister Camille Opens Specialised Training on Maritime Safety and Search and Rescue

The Minister for Homeland Security and Civil Affairs,Mr.  James Camille, officially opened a five-day Specialised Course on Maritime Safety and Search and Rescue Challenges at Sea yesterday morning.

The training is organised in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration (IOM), Naif Arab University for Security Sciences, the Regional Maritime Information Fusion Centre (RMFIC), the Regional Coordination Operations Centre (RCOC) and the Government of Seychelles.

The programme focuses on the functions of the regional centres, maritime security challenges facing Seychelles and the wider Western Indian Ocean region, as well as strengthening coordination and response capabilities during incidents at sea.

For Seychelles, as a small island nation with a vast maritime area of responsibility, effective search and rescue operations and regional cooperation are essential to safeguarding lives at sea.

The five-day course provides an opportunity for participants to exchange expertise and strengthen collaboration in advancing maritime safety and security.

stories.description: Wavel Ramkalawan won the Seychelles presidential election on 25 October 2020, securing 54.9% of the vote against incumbent Danny Faure’s 43.5%. The result ended more than four decades of rule by the former single-party government, according to the publication.

publications.text:
📅 25 OCTOBER | THIS DAY IN AFRICAN HISTORY

🇺🇬 1962: UGANDA TOOK ITS PLACE AT THE UNITED NATIONS

On 25 October 1962, Uganda was officially admitted to the United Nations.

The country had gained independence from Britain just 16 days earlier, on 9 October.

Its admission to the UN represented an important moment in Uganda’s history.

For decades, decisions affecting Uganda’s future had been made under British colonial administration.

Now, as an independent nation, Uganda could participate directly in international discussions and decisions.

It became the 110th member of the United Nations.

This was also a remarkable period in African history.

Across the continent, newly independent countries were joining international institutions and demanding a greater voice in global affairs.

African countries were increasingly able to influence discussions about colonialism, development, peace and international cooperation.

Today marks 64 years since Uganda joined the United Nations.

It is a reminder that political independence was only one part of Africa’s transformation.

Having a voice in international affairs was another.

🇪🇹 2018: ETHIOPIA ELECTED ITS FIRST WOMAN PRESIDENT

On 25 October 2018, Ethiopia made history.

The country’s parliament unanimously elected Sahle-Work Zewde as its first woman president.

And her appointment was significant for several reasons.

Sahle-Work was an experienced diplomat who had represented Ethiopia internationally and held senior positions within the United Nations.

She had served as Ethiopia’s ambassador to several countries and headed the United Nations Office at Nairobi.

Before becoming president, she was the UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative to the African Union.

Her appointment came during a period of political reforms in Ethiopia.

Just days earlier, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed had appointed a cabinet in which half the ministers were women.

Although Ethiopia’s presidency is largely ceremonial, with executive authority held by the prime minister, Sahle-Work’s appointment was an important symbolic achievement.

She became the first woman to hold the presidency in modern Ethiopia.

In her inaugural address, she emphasised the importance of peace, unity and women’s rights.

Her appointment challenged assumptions about women’s place in political leadership.

Sahle-Work served as president until October 2024.

Today marks eight years since her historic election.

Her story reminds us that African women have contributed to diplomacy, international relations and political leadership at the highest levels.

🇪🇹 2015: ETHIOPIAN ATHLETES MADE MARATHON HISTORY IN GERMANY

On 25 October 2015, two Ethiopian athletes achieved something remarkable at the Frankfurt Marathon in Germany.

Sisay Lemma won the men’s race in 2 hours, 6 minutes and 26 seconds.

But there was another Ethiopian victory that day.

Gulume Tollesa won the women’s race in 2 hours, 23 minutes and 12 seconds.

It was the first time Ethiopian athletes had won both the men’s and women’s titles at the Frankfurt Marathon in the same year.

And Tollesa’s victory was particularly dramatic.

She finished in a sprint against fellow Ethiopian Dinkinesh Mekash.

Both women were credited with exactly the same finishing time.

Tollesa won by the narrowest of margins.

The result demonstrated the extraordinary depth of Ethiopia’s distance-running talent.

Ethiopian athletes have become internationally recognised for their achievements in long-distance running.

But behind those victories are years of training, discipline and determination.

Today marks 11 years since that historic Ethiopian double.

It is another achievement worth remembering when celebrating African sporting excellence.

🇸🇨 2020: SEYCHELLES EXPERIENCED A HISTORIC DEMOCRATIC TRANSITION

On 25 October 2020, the results of Seychelles’ presidential election were announced.

And they marked a turning point in the country’s political history.

Seychelles is an African island nation in the Indian Ocean.

Since 1977, its presidency had remained under the control of the same political movement.

But in October 2020, voters chose a different direction.

Opposition candidate Wavel Ramkalawan won the presidential election with approximately 54.9% of the vote.

He defeated incumbent president Danny Faure, who received approximately 43.5%.

Ramkalawan had previously contested several presidential elections without success.

His victory represented the first time an opposition candidate had won the presidency since Seychelles gained independence in 1976.

And there was something particularly important about what happened next.

The outgoing president accepted the result.

Ramkalawan called for national reconciliation, emphasising that Seychellois citizens needed to move forward together.

The election demonstrated that political power could change hands peacefully through democratic institutions.

Seychelles experienced another peaceful electoral change in 2025, when Patrick Herminie defeated Ramkalawan.

Today marks six years since the historic 2020 result.

It remains an important chapter in the democratic history of this African island nation.

🌍 TODAY’S REFLECTION

Today’s stories remind us that African progress takes many forms.

Uganda’s admission to the United Nations strengthened its international voice.

Sahle-Work Zewde’s election challenged barriers facing women in political leadership.

Ethiopian athletes demonstrated extraordinary excellence on the international sporting stage.

And voters in Seychelles showed that political leadership could change through the ballot box.

Different countries. Different generations. Different achievements.

But each story reveals something about Africans shaping their own futures.

Which of these achievements do you believe has made the greatest contribution to Africa’s progress, and why?

📅 24 OCTOBER | THIS DAY IN AFRICAN HISTORY

🇿🇲 1964: ZAMBIA CELEBRATES ITS INDEPENDENCE

On 24 October 1964, Zambia gained independence from British colonial rule.

Previously known as Northern Rhodesia, the country became an independent republic, with Kenneth Kaunda as its first president.

But Zambia’s independence was important far beyond its borders.

Under Kaunda, the country became a centre of support for liberation movements fighting colonial and white minority rule across southern Africa.

Movements from South Africa, Zimbabwe, Namibia and other countries received political support and refuge in Zambia.

This came at a considerable cost, as Zambia faced economic and security pressures because of its position.

Kaunda’s domestic political record was more complicated, particularly after Zambia became a one-party state.

Nevertheless, Zambia’s contribution to the liberation of southern Africa remains an important part of its history.

Today marks 62 years of Zambian independence.

Happy Independence Day to the people of Zambia!

🇪🇬 1973: THE PEOPLE OF SUEZ RESISTED DURING THE OCTOBER WAR

On 24 October 1973, Egyptian civilians and security forces resisted Israeli troops during the October War.

The fighting took place around Suez, an Egyptian city near the southern end of the Suez Canal.

The October War had begun on 6 October, when Egyptian and Syrian forces launched attacks against Israeli positions.

By 24 October, despite international efforts to establish a ceasefire, fighting continued around Suez.

Egyptian resistance fighters, supported by soldiers and police, confronted Israeli forces attempting to take control of the city.

Their resistance became an important symbol of Egyptian determination.

Today, Suez Governorate commemorates 24 October as its National Day.

The anniversary honours those who defended the city during one of the most significant conflicts in modern Egyptian history.

Today marks 53 years since that resistance.

🇰🇪 2018: ELIUD KIPCHOGE RECEIVED A UNITED NATIONS AWARD

On 24 October 2018, Kenyan marathon champion Eliud Kipchoge was honoured as the United Nations in Kenya Person of the Year.

The award recognised more than his achievements in athletics.

Just weeks earlier, Kipchoge had broken the men’s marathon world record at the Berlin Marathon, completing the race in 2 hours, 1 minute and 39 seconds.

But the United Nations also recognised his commitment to inspiring young people and supporting efforts to address HIV/AIDS in Kenya.

Kipchoge had become an international symbol of discipline, perseverance and determination.

His message was that extraordinary achievements come through years of consistent effort.

The award was presented during celebrations marking United Nations Day in Nairobi.

Today marks eight years since Kipchoge received the honour.

His story reminds us that African sporting excellence can influence lives far beyond the competition itself.

🇸🇨 2020: SEYCHELLES HELD AN ELECTION THAT CHANGED ITS POLITICAL HISTORY

On 24 October 2020, voting concluded in a historic presidential and parliamentary election in Seychelles.

Seychelles is an island nation in the Indian Ocean, off the eastern coast of Africa.

Since 1977, the country’s presidency had remained in the hands of the same political movement.

But the election of October 2020 brought a remarkable change.

The following day, election officials announced that opposition candidate Wavel Ramkalawan had won the presidency with approximately 54.9% of the vote.

He defeated incumbent President Danny Faure.

It was the first time an opposition candidate had won the presidency since Seychelles gained independence in 1976.

The opposition also secured a substantial parliamentary majority.

The election demonstrated that political power could change hands through the ballot box.

Today marks six years since voting concluded in that historic election.

It remains an important chapter in the democratic history of this African island nation.

🌍 TODAY’S REFLECTION

Today’s stories celebrate different forms of African courage and achievement.

Zambia’s independence strengthened the wider struggle for African liberation.

The people of Suez demonstrated resistance during a difficult period of war.

Eliud Kipchoge showed how sporting excellence can inspire future generations.

And voters in Seychelles demonstrated the power of democratic participation.

Which of these stories do you believe deserves greater recognition in African history, and why?

stories.title: Patrick Herminie Resumes Duties After Medical Leave
stories.description: In a statement published on 28 October 2026, Patrick Herminie said he was back at State House after medical leave and fit to resume presidential duties, adding that he would remain president until 2030. He described attention to his health as “a storm in a teacup” and alleged that anonymous and fake accounts amplified claims about his illness, with some wishing for his death to force new elections.

publications.text:
President Patrick Herminie is back at State House after medical leave: "I am fit to resume duty. I will be President until 2030." He called the attention on his health "a storm in a teacup" and said government is delivering in all sectors. 

Herminie says critics used anonymous and fake accounts to inflate his illness, some even wishing for his death to force new elections. #Seychelles 

https://t.co/Da48iexM1H

“I am fit to resume duty tomorrow. I will be President until 2030.” — President Herminie

President of the Republic Dr Patrick Herminie resumes official duties tomorrow, Wednesday 28 October, following a period of medical leave during which he was admitted to the Seychelles Hospital.

Speaking to the State House Press Office, the President described the attention around his health as “a storm in a teacup.”

He said the Government is delivering across all sectors, and that some opponents, with little else to challenge, have exaggerated his illness, much of it through anonymous and fake social media profiles.

The President noted that most Seychellois understand illness is part of being human. Wishing harm on others, he said, goes against the values we learnt from our elders. He expressed regret that some individuals had used his illness for political ends, with some going as far as wishing for his death to trigger fresh elections.

The President also explained what the Constitution provides should a sitting President die in office.

He thanked everyone who kept him in their thoughts and prayers.

(Source: State House)

publications.title: Vice-President Pillay to Represent Seychelles at COP31 Leaders' Summit in Türkiye from 11 to 12 November
publications.text:
Vice-President Pillay to Represent Seychelles at COP31 Leaders' Summit in Türkiye from 11 to 12 November

Vice-President Mr Sebastien Pillay will represent Seychelles at the COP31 Leaders' Summit in Antalya, Türkiye. The two-day high-level gathering brings together world leaders to address pressing global climate challenges, set political direction and build momentum ahead of the negotiations that follow.

As a Small Island Developing State (SIDS), Seychelles remains particularly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, including rising sea levels, coastal erosion and extreme weather events. The summit will provide an important platform for Seychelles to highlight the challenges faced by island nations and advocate for stronger international cooperation, improved access to climate financing and greater support for climate adaptation.

COP31 will feature a historic leadership arrangement, with Türkiye hosting and presiding over the conference, while Australia leads the formal negotiations. This marks the first time such a shared leadership structure has been adopted in the history of the United Nations Climate Change Conferences.

Seychelles' participation reflects its continued engagement in international climate discussions and its commitment to advancing the interests of SIDS, particularly in addressing the disproportionate impacts of climate change on vulnerable nations.

Vice-President Pillay is scheduled to depart Seychelles on Tuesday, 10 November, and return on Saturday, 14 November.

stories.title: Seychelles Seeks Grenada's Support for Venn's Town (Seychelles) Bid
stories.description: The Seychelles Times reported on 2 November 2026 that Seychelles was seeking Grenada's support for the Venn's Town (Seychelles) World Heritage bid. It said Seychelles' Minister for Foreign Affairs and the Diaspora (Barry Faure) met Grenada's Minister of Tourism, Creative Economy and Culture (Senator Adrian Thomas) on the margins of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 2026 in Antigua and Barbuda; the meeting date and any outcome are unspecified.

publications.text:
Seychelles and Grenada Discuss Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation

Minister for Foreign Affairs and the Diaspora, Mr Barry Faure, met with Grenada’s Minister of Tourism, Creative Economy and Culture, Senator Adrian Thomas, on the margins of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) 2026 being held in Antigua and Barbuda.

The discussions focused on the importance of strengthening solidarity and cooperation among Small Island Developing States (SIDS), particularly in promoting cultural heritage. The Ministers exchanged views on the common vulnerabilities faced by their respective countries including their dependence on exports and tourism and the impact of external shocks and geopolitical developments on tourism flows.

During the meeting, Minister Faure sought Grenada’s support for Seychelles’ efforts to secure UNESCO World Heritage recognition for Venn’s Town, an important national historical site and tourist attraction. He highlighted the site's significant cultural and ecological value to Seychelles, noting that its recognition would complement the country’s two existing UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Aldabra Atoll and Vallée de Mai, located on Praslin Island.

Follow the below link to read more:
https://mfa.gov.sc/news/seychelles-and-grenada-discuss-strengthening-bilateral-cooperation/

[IPS] Victoria, Seychelles -- On 21 September 1976, less than three months after independence, Seychelles took its seat in the General Assembly of the United Nations. We became the 145th member of the Organisation. For a young nation of scattered islands in the Indian Ocean, with a small population and no army to speak of, it was far more than a ceremony. stories.title: Poaching Alleged at St Anne Marine Reserve (Seychelles)
stories.description: In a Facebook post published on 13 October 2026, the publisher says they witnessed a boat named ST PAUL, registration SZ. 756, dropping fish cages and retrieving one containing assorted fish in St Anne Marine Reserve (Seychelles), between St Anne Island (Seychelles) and Moyenne Island (Seychelles); the date of the incident is not specified. The publisher says they and another boat were threatened with a large knife when they confronted the alleged poacher, and alleges the Seychelles Parks and Gardens Authority did not respond to a hotline report for about an hour and later directed them to report the matter to police.

publications.text:
St Anne Marine reserve is being exploited by un-policed poachers!
Sadly we witnessed a poacher in his boat ST PAUL Reg no: SZ. 756 dropping fish cages and retrieve one full of a variety of fish between St Anne and Moyenne island . 

We confronted the poacher only to be threatened with a large knife . Another boat also approached him and reportedly faced the same threats. 

We learn that the other boat reported him immediately to Seychelles Parks and Gardens Authority (SPGA) hotline but we saw no one come out to investigate for the next hour or so whilst the poacher brazenly continued with his illegal actions.

We reported it to the SPGA by email later in the day (including providing photos) to now be told we have to go to the Police and formally report this . 

We are on a short holiday & naturally don’t have time for this nor to come back for any court case.

This individual can easily be traced from the boat name and registration number and should at least get a warning for his offence to stop him continuing this exploitation of a nature reserve.

The  SPGA are not doing their job adequately in monitoring these areas nor reacting to offenders being reported. If this continues, there will be no more fish in the Reserve and Seychelles tourism will suffer as a result.

Maybe Club Med could sponsor a lookout who monitors the area by binoculars and reports to a reactive policing party?

A solution needs to be found before it is too late.

Please share if you agree

stories.title: Two Men Remanded in Hyundai i10 Theft Case
stories.description: Police said Naizer Esparon, 17, and Sandro Tamboo, 18, were formally charged at the Magistrates’ Court on Ile du Port (Seychelles) on 4 November 2026 in connection with a Hyundai i10 stolen from a petrol station in Point Larue (Seychelles) on 15 October 2026. The court set bail conditions, but both were remanded after failing to meet the bail payments; Tamboo was sent to Montagne Posee Prison and Esparon to the juvenile prison on Praslin (Seychelles).

publications.text:

21.10.2026

Kominike (Swivi)

De sispe zonm enn aze 17an sorti Union Vale e lot 18an sorti Perseverance, in pas devan Lakour Mazistra Ile du Port ozordi apremidi, kot zot in ganny rimann an detansyon lapolis pour 14 zour.

Sa i an koneksyon avek lanket ki lapolis pe fer dan plizyer ka vol ek andomaz propriyete. Sa bann ka i konsern de transpor Hyundai i10 ki ti ganny raporte vole. Premye transpor ti ganny raporte vole le 15 Oktob 2026 kot stasyon petrol Point Larue, tandis ki dezyenm ti ganny raporte vole le 20 Oktob 2026 dan rezyon Union Vale.

Pandan en loperasyon ki lapolis ti fer yerswar, bann zofisye ti reisi entersepte enn parmi sa bann transpor Mont Buxton, kot enn parmi bann sispe ti ganny arete sirplas.

Lapolis i annan rezon pour krwar ki serten pyes sa de transpor ti ganny retire e monte lo sa transpor ki ti ganny sezi. Lanket i ankor an progre dan sa bann ka.

Sa i an rapor avek en transpor Hyundai i10 ki ti ganny vole kot stasyon petrol Point Larue le 15 Oktob 2026.

Mazistra in larg tou le de akize lo serten kondisyon, parmi ki i enkli peyman en kosyon larzan.

Esparon in ganny large lo en kosyon 8mil roupi e i bezwen osi prodwir en dimoun koman en garanti pour en sonm 10mil roupi. I bezwen osi sinny liv Lakour kot kordgard Perseverance trwa fwa par semenn, pa komet okenn lofans similer e pa enterfer avek konplenan oubyen okenn temwen dan sa ka.

Me vi ki tou le de akize pann reisi satisfer demann Lakour an sa ki konsern peyman zot kosyon, zot in ganny rimann an detansyon Servis Prizon Sesel. Tamboo in ganny rimann Prizon Montagne Posee, tandis ki Esparon in ganny rimann prizon pour bann miner lo zil Praslin.

publications.text:
Bann manm Sekirite Prezidansyel in amelyor zot konpetans dan proteksyon Sef Leta, apre ki zot in konplet premye faz en progranm formasyon entansif kin ale pour 6 mwan.

Avek zot leksperyans ek konpetans ki zot deza annan, sa bann zofisye in ganny bann nouvo teknik avanse ki lo standar enternasyonal, pour ranforsi zot kapasite ek preparasyon pour reazir fas avek nenport ki menas.

Bomaten, Prezidan Larepiblik, Dr Patrick Herminie, ki osi Komandan an Sef Lafors Defans Sesel, in asiste en seri legzersis similasyon kot sa bann zofisye in demontre bann konpetans ki zot in gannyen pandan sa formasyon. Sa bann legzersis in osi mark lafen premye faz sa progranm.

Prezidan Herminie ti ganny akonpannyen par Sef Lafors Defans, Mazor Zeneral Michael Rosette; Sef Deta-Mazor, Kolonel Michael Hollanda; ek Komandan Linite Operasyon Spesyal, Lyetnan Kolonel Archille Mondon.

Sa bann legzersis ti konsantre prensipalman lo proteksyon raprose, kot bann zofisye ti bezwen reazir fas avek diferan senaryo menas kont en personnaz anba proteksyon. Zot in demontre bann teknik defans kont latak avek kouto ek fizi, kot zot ti bezwen azir vitman pour protez sa personnaz, dezarm bann agreser e evakye li an sekirite. Bann zofisye in osi demontre zot kapasite pour donn premye swen e tret bann blesir dan bann sityasyon kot i annan bokou presyon. An plis ki sa, zot in montre zot konpetans dan litilizasyon drone pour sirveyans e pour annan en pli bon vizibilite ek konprenezon bann sityasyon lo teren. Sa formasyon i form parti en progranm korperasyon kontinyel ant Larepiblik Sesel ek Federasyon Larisi, dan domenn ranforsman kapasite defans ek sekirite.

publications.title: Presidential Security Strengthened as First Phase of Training Concludes
publications.text:
Presidential Security Strengthened as First Phase of Training Concludes

Members of the Presidential Security have sharpened their skills in protecting the Head of State, completing the first phase of an intensive six-month training programme. Building on their existing expertise, officers have acquired advanced techniques of an international standard, further enhancing their readiness to respond to any threat.

This morning, President Dr Patrick Herminie, Commander-in-Chief of the Seychelles Defence Forces, witnessed a series of simulation exercises demonstrating these skills and marking the end of the first phase. He was accompanied by the Chief of Defence Forces, Major General Michael Rosette; the Chief of Staff, Colonel Michael Hollanda; and the Commanding Officer of the Special Operations Unit, Lieutenant Colonel Archille Mondon.

The exercises focused on close protection, with officers responding to simulated threats against a protected person. They demonstrated defensive techniques against knife and firearm attacks, moving swiftly to shield, disarm and evacuate. Officers also showed their ability to administer first aid and treat injuries under pressure, and to deploy drones for surveillance and situational awareness.

Expressing his satisfaction with the programme, President Herminie said he was proud to see Seychellois officers performing to such a high international standard.

Major General Rosette said that, with the first phase now complete, members of the Presidential Security are better equipped to carry out their duties.

The training forms part of ongoing defence and security capacity-building cooperation between the Republic of Seychelles and the Russian Federation.

Sharper. Stronger. Ready.

Our Presidential Security has completed the first phase of an intensive six-month training programme, gaining advanced, international-standard skills in close protection, defence, first aid and drone surveillance.

stories.title: AfCRA Includes Seychelles in Sovereign Rating Discussions
stories.description: AfCRA interim director-general Sifiso Falala said in a Reuters interview on 3 November 2026 that the agency was discussing analyses with 15 states, including Seychelles. He said AfCRA expected to publish its first ratings in several countries by the end of March 2027; the publication does not say whether Seychelles will be among them.

publications.text:
Africa's New Credit Rating Agency in Talks With 15 Sovereigns: Media 

AfCRA aims to publish its first ratings by March, according to interim CEO Sifiso Falala, cited by the media.

👉 Staff from the Mauritius-based agency will conduct research in countries including Togo, Kenya, Seychelles, Burundi, and Mauritius, he added.

ℹ️ Launched last month, privately owned AfCRA challenges the big three rating firms, which African leaders say overstate lending risks in Africa and downgrade countries too quickly during periods of stress.

🌍 **L’agence africaine de notation **[**publiera ses premières notes avant la fin mars 2027**](https://afrinz.ru/fr/?p=364173&preview=true)

L’Agence africaine de notation de crédit (AfCRA), créée en guise d’alternative aux grandes agences mondiales de notation, prévoit de publier ses premières notes dans plusieurs pays d’ici à la fin du mois de mars 2027. C’est ce qu’a indiqué le 3 novembre, dans un entretien à l’agence Reuters, son directeur général par intérim, Sifiso Falala.

🔸 Selon lui, les collaborateurs de l’agence sont en discussion avec quinze États, dont le Togo, le Kenya, les Seychelles, le Burundi et Maurice, en vue de réaliser des analyses.

« Nous serons en mesure, d’ici mars, avant la fin du mois de mars, d’avoir publié des résultats », a relevé Sifiso Falala.

🔸 Il a expliqué que l’approche de l’AfCRA en matière d’évaluation de la solvabilité des États devait permettre de porter un autre regard sur les économies africaines. Selon son directeur général, l’agence attribuera des notes à la demande des États eux-mêmes et mènera également des analyses sur les institutions multilatérales africaines, dont Afreximbank, et sur des établissements financiers privés.

stories.title: US Orders Financial-Transfer Ban on MEXC Global
stories.description: On 6 November 2026, FinCEN issued an order barring banks, broker-dealers and money transmitters from sending funds to or from MEXC Global and its foreign subsidiaries, branches and offices. FinCEN says MEXC handled more than $16 billion in illicit transactions; the restriction takes effect 30 days after Federal Register publication, which the publication said had not appeared as of 6 November 2026.

publications.text:
US Treasury sanctions eight Canadian currency-exchange businesses

The US Treasury announced sanctions on eight Canadian currency-exchange businesses on Friday, November 6, making the number of targeted firms the clearest measure of the action’s scale. The Treasury accused the businesses of assisting Iranian entities in getting around US financial sanctions. The action was presented under the Treasury’s “Operation Economic Outcast” designation, which identifies the campaign as the stated framework for these measures. The Treasury said some of the firms changed Iranian rials and other currencies into digital assets, with cryptocurrency among the forms it identified. The allegations describe a chain that begins with currency conversion and involves digital assets, while the Treasury’s stated concern is the alleged evasion of US financial sanctions on behalf of Iranian entities. The action therefore targets alleged financial activity rather than describing a general restriction on all currency exchange businesses in Canada; the sanctions apply to the firms named by the Treasury.

The eight businesses named by the Treasury are Diverse Trade Inc, 1380079 BC Limited, Top PC Technician Inc and NIA Nations Currency Ltd. The remaining named firms are 2397639 Ontario Ltd, CCC Inc, B Galaxy Inc and Darvish Exchange. The reporting places the businesses in Ontario and British Columbia, identifying their provincial locations rather than giving a count for each province. Taken together, the names make clear that the action covers multiple separately identified businesses, rather than one company operating under a single name. The provincial information locates the affected businesses in two parts of Canada, but the reporting does not specify how many of the named firms are in either province. That distinction matters because the location information describes where the firms are based, while the sanctions themselves are announced against the named businesses.

The Treasury alleged that some of the businesses dealt with Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges already under US sanctions. It also alleged links between some firms and digital-wallet addresses associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, or IRGC. A supported synthesis of the reporting is that the firms face allegations involving both sanctions evasion for Iranian entities and money linked to an alleged drug-trafficking operation. The allegations about exchanges and wallet addresses add detail to the Treasury’s account of how some firms may have interacted with entities or addresses connected to Iran. The reporting does not say that every one of the named businesses engaged in each alleged activity; it attributes these dealings to some firms and the money links to several designated businesses. The two strands of allegations are distinct: one concerns Iranian entities and sanctioned exchanges, while the other concerns money linked to an alleged trafficking network.

The sanctions freeze any assets the firms hold in the United States and prohibit transactions with American people or entities. These restrictions address property and dealings connected to the United States, as described in the account of the measures. The reported effects concern the sanctioned firms and their potential US assets or transactions; the source does not provide a total value for assets frozen. The freeze applies to assets the firms hold in the United States, whereas the transaction bar concerns dealings with American people or entities. Those are two different practical consequences of the sanctions: property may be frozen, and transactions involving the specified American parties are barred. The available account sets out the types of property and dealings affected, but does not say whether any particular firm holds assets in the United States or identify specific transactions. As a result, the stated restrictions are clear even though the reporting does not quantify their financial effect on the businesses.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Canada should not serve as a refuge for financial intermediaries helping Iran and its proxies evade sanctions. The Treasury also said its broader sanctions campaign is intended to cut off economic support for the Iranian regime and the IRGC. Bessent’s statement sets out the US government’s view of the risk: financial facilitators based in Canada should not help Iran or its proxies get around sanctions. The campaign’s stated goal reaches beyond the firms in this action, framing sanctions as a way to disrupt economic support for the Iranian regime and the IRGC. These are statements of policy and purpose; the reporting does not establish that the measures have already severed those economic lifelines.

FINTRAC said it worked with the US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, known as FinCEN, in imposing the measures against the money-service businesses. FINTRAC also described its broader practice of cooperating with foreign financial intelligence units. The account thus identifies cooperation between Canadian and US financial-crime agencies in this particular action, while also describing FINTRAC’s regular international work. FINTRAC said that its work with foreign intelligence units addresses money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions evasion, placing the cooperation in a wider enforcement context. The reporting describes FINTRAC as a partner in the process, but does not give details about what information each agency contributed.

The Treasury also alleged that several of the designated businesses handled money connected to Ryan Wedding, a former Canadian Olympic snowboarder accused of heading an international drug-trafficking network. US authorities said businesses in the Toronto and Vancouver areas converted drug proceeds into digital assets and sent them abroad. These allegations add a drug-proceeds dimension to the account of the businesses, alongside the claims about Iranian entities and cryptocurrency exchanges. The reported conversion of proceeds into digital assets and their transfer abroad describes the alleged movement of funds, but the account does not identify which individual businesses performed each step. Wedding is described as accused of leading the network, not as having been convicted in the facts provided here. The distinction between allegation and established outcome is important: the reporting attributes the claims to the Treasury and US authorities and describes the trafficking network as alleged.

In a separate action, FinCEN issued an order aimed at MEXC Global, a cryptocurrency exchange incorporated in Seychelles. That order bars US financial institutions from processing transfers of funds involving MEXC Global. FinCEN said the exchange had facilitated at least $16bn in illicit transactions associated with Iran, North Korea, Russia and other sanctioned actors. The MEXC Global order focuses on a cryptocurrency exchange and the ability of US financial institutions to process transfers involving it; it is not the same measure as the sanctions against the Canadian businesses. FinCEN’s estimate of at least $16bn concerns transactions it said the exchange facilitated, not the value of assets frozen under the Canadian-firm sanctions. The actors cited in connection with those transactions include Iran, North Korea and Russia, as well as other sanctioned actors, so the reported activity spans more than one country. The order’s practical restriction is on US financial institutions processing transfers, while the reported transaction figure describes the scale FinCEN attributed to illicit activity.

A supported synthesis of the reporting is that the Canadian-firm sanctions and the MEXC Global order are separate actions, although both concern alleged illicit financial activity involving Iran. The actions differ in their targets and stated restrictions: one names Canadian money-service businesses and freezes their US assets while barring specified transactions, and the other concerns a Seychelles-incorporated exchange and transfer processing by US financial institutions. Their overlap is the reported connection to alleged illicit financial activity involving Iran; the two measures should not be read as one joint case or as actions against the same businesses. The reporting also presents the Canadian-firm allegations as concerning both Iranian sanctions evasion and funds linked to an alleged drug-trafficking operation, while the MEXC Global figure concerns illicit transactions associated with several sanctioned actors. Together, the accounts show different enforcement tools being applied to different targets, without establishing that the firms and exchange were part of one network.

**US Treasury Orders Financial Institutions to Cut Off MEXC Exchange**

The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has issued an order directing American financial institutions to stop processing fund transfers to or from MEXC Exchange.

FinCEN alleges the platform facilitated at least $16 billion in transactions linked to sanctions evasion, cybercrime, and other illicit activity. The transactions in question span the period from May 2021 to May 2026, according to the order.

The action effectively cuts MEXC off from the US financial system, placing it alongside a small number of exchanges that have faced similar Treasury-level enforcement. MEXC is registered in the Seychelles and has not held a US operating license.

[Source](https://www.thecoinrepublic.com/2026/11/07/mexc-exchange-faces-us-treasury-order-over-16b-in-illicit-transactions/)

**Il Tesoro USA taglia fuori l'exchange MEXC dal sistema finanziario americano**

L'autorità antiriciclaggio americana FinCEN ha designato l'exchange MEXC Global come istituto di „primaria preoccupazione per riciclaggio". Le banche statunitensi non potranno più gestire trasferimenti che coinvolgono MEXC. La misura entrerà in vigore 30 giorni dopo la pubblicazione nella Gazzetta ufficiale.

Secondo FinCEN, l'exchange con sede alle Seychelles ha gestito tra il 2021 e il 2026 almeno 16 miliardi di dollari di transazioni illecite. Tra queste circa 1,5 miliardi per aggirare le sanzioni contro la Russia, circa 1 miliardo con oltre 40 exchange iraniani e circa 2 miliardi legati al crimine informatico.

Da notare: si tratta di conclusioni dell'autorità, non di una sentenza. MEXC sta esaminando l'ordine, resta operativa e ha avviato una verifica indipendente dei propri controlli.

**Il Tesoro USA taglia fuori l'exchange MEXC dal sistema finanziario americano**

L'autorità antiriciclaggio americana FinCEN ha designato l'exchange MEXC Global come istituto di „primaria preoccupazione per riciclaggio". Le banche statunitensi non potranno più gestire trasferimenti che coinvolgono MEXC. La misura entrerà in vigore 30 giorni dopo la pubblicazione nella Gazzetta ufficiale.

Secondo FinCEN, l'exchange con sede alle Seychelles ha gestito tra il 2021 e il 2026 almeno 16 miliardi di dollari di transazioni illecite. Tra queste circa 1,5 miliardi per aggirare le sanzioni contro la Russia, circa 1 miliardo con oltre 40 exchange iraniani e circa 2 miliardi legati al crimine informatico.

Da notare: si tratta di conclusioni dell'autorità, non di una sentenza. MEXC sta esaminando l'ordine, resta operativa e ha avviato una verifica indipendente dei propri controlli.

The US is moving to cut a major offshore exchange off from American banks without sanctioning it.

FinCEN says MEXC handled more than $16B in illicit transactions. The tool it used is the story.

What the November 6 order does
• Issued under Section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act, which draws on the Section 311 framework
• Bars banks, broker-dealers and money transmitters from transmitting funds to or from MEXC Global and covers its foreign subsidiaries, branches and offices
• It is not an OFAC SDN designation. No property is blocked and no accounts are frozen
• It takes effect 30 days after Federal Register publication, and none had appeared as of Friday evening

Treasury is using a Russia-focused money laundering authority to pull a Seychelles-linked exchange that isn't licensed in the US off US financial rails. FinCEN used similar transmittal bans on Mexican institutions under the FEND Off Fentanyl Act. Other offshore exchanges may see the same treatment.

The dollar system runs on permission. Bitcoin doesn't.

New ice plant opens in Bel Ombre to support local fishers

by R. Julie 

Fishers from Bel Ombre and the surrounding areas now have access to a new ice plant following its official opening by the Seychelles Fisheries Authority (SFA) on Monday, with support from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the Government of Japan.

𝐋𝐈𝐕𝐄 𝐔𝐏𝐃𝐀𝐓𝐄:
Opening of the Bel Ombre Ice plant
(Credit: Gilliana Anacoura)

🔵 New Ice Plant Inaugurated at Bel Ombre!

The Seychelles Fisheries Authority (SFA) officially inaugurated its new ice plant facility at Bel Ombre yesterday afternoon, in a move to better support the local fishing community.

It was the Minister for Fisheries, Agriculture and the Blue Economy, Mr Wallace Cosgrow, SFA Chief Executive Officer, Dr Jan Robinson, and Principal Secretary for Agriculture, Mr Keven Nancy, who cut the ribbon to officially open the facility.

The new plant has the capacity to produce 5 tonnes every 24 hours and can store up to 7 tonnes of ice.

Donated by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the Government of Japan under the Reef Fish Project, the facility will improve access to ice for local fishers, allowing them to obtain sufficient supplies more conveniently.

Fishermen attending the inauguration welcomed the facility and expressed their appreciation for the support it will bring to their daily work.

With the use of the new facility, SFA will be able to do maintenance work on the previously existing facility, which has been serving the fishing community in this region for many years. Once the work is completed, both facilities will be in use, increasing the supply of ice that fishers can access.

This initiative is an important step towards strengthening fishers’ livelihoods, enhancing food security and promoting sustainable fisheries in Seychelles. 🇸🇨🌊

stories.title: Officials Review Assistance for La Digue (Seychelles) Flooding
stories.description: On 21 October 2026, Secretary of State for Lands, Housing and Infrastructure Joseph Francois, MNA Rocky Uranie, District Administrator Barbara Barallon and other stakeholders visited residents affected by recent flooding on La Digue (Seychelles). They reviewed progress and discussed further assistance and works to address outstanding concerns; the flooding date and extent are not specified.

publications.text:
Working with residents to address flooding on La Digue

Secretary of State for Lands, Housing and Infrastructure Joseph Francois led a visit to La Digue to assess the impact of recent flooding and help affected households.

Joined by representatives of the Seychelles Infrastructure Agency, the District Administrator and the Member of the National Assembly for Inner Islands, Hon. Rocky Uranie, the team stayed on site till late, meeting residents, listening to their concerns and discussing practical ways to assist them.

Decisions taken during the visit helped guide actions to reduce the flooding. Water levels have since receded considerably, allowing affected residents to begin returning to their daily routines.

Thank you to the residents for their patience, cooperation and for sharing their concerns with the team. Work will continue early tomorrow morning.

Secretary of State for Lands, Housing and Infrastructure Joseph Francois was again on the ground on La Digue today, accompanied by MNA Hon. Rocky Uranie, District Administrator Barbara Barallon and other stakeholders. The team visited residents affected by the recent flooding, reviewed progress and discussed further assistance and works needed to address outstanding concerns.

stories.title: Seychelles Defence Forces Assist IFB Sajira
stories.description: On 2 October 2026, the High Commission of India expressed gratitude to the Government of Seychelles, particularly the Seychelles Defence Forces, for swift support and assistance to the vessel IFB Sajira and her crew. It described the assistance as reflecting longstanding bilateral defence and maritime ties; the assistance’s date, nature and location are not specified.

publications.text:
Government of India expresses gratitude to the Government of Seychelles for its swift and life-saving assistance to 17 Indian fishermen aboard IFB Sajira, which suffered an engine failure in the high seas off the coast of Seychelles.

This timely assistance reflects the close and enduring bonds of friendship between India and Seychelles, and our shared commitment to the safety and well-being of our people. 

🇮🇳🇸🇨

The High Commission of India expresses its sincere gratitude to the Government of Seychelles, in particular, the Seychelles Defence Forces for their swift support and assistance to the vessel IFB Sajira and her crew.

This act stands as a  testimony to our long-standing friendship and deep-rooted bilateral defence and maritime ties.

stories.title: Seychelles Highlights Solar Investment Priorities at ISA Assembly
stories.description: At the Ninth International Solar Alliance Assembly in New Delhi (India), running 2–5 November 2026, Seychelles highlighted financing solar projects and applying solar technology in agriculture as priorities. Minister for Industry and Enterprise Geralda Desaubin represented Seychelles; the item was published on 4 November 2026.

publications.text:
The Minister for Industry and Enterprise, Ms Geralda Desaubin, is representing Seychelles at the Ninth Session of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) Assembly, taking place in New Delhi, India, from 2nd to 5th November 2026.

The Assembly brings together member countries and key stakeholders to strengthen international cooperation, mobilise investment and accelerate the global transition towards affordable and sustainable solar energy. The official opening ceremony featured an address by the Chief Guest, the Honourable Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India.

During the Assembly, Minister Desaubin addressed the gathering on behalf of Seychelles, in its capacity as Chair of the ISA Regional Committee for Africa. Her address focused on the report of the Committee’s Eighth Meeting, held on 26th August 2026 in Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe, under the chairmanship of Ms Marie-May Jeremie, Seychelles’ Minister responsible for Environment, Climate, Energy and Natural Resources.

In presenting the report, Minister Desaubin highlighted three key developments: the Solarising Africa Initiative, which provides an implementation blueprint for the continent’s clean energy transition; the Africa Solar Facility, a US$200 million blended-finance initiative aimed at mobilising private investment in decentralised renewable energy; and efforts to promote solar-powered agriculture through water pumping systems and agrivoltaic technologies.

For Seychelles, participation in the Assembly provides an important opportunity to strengthen international partnerships, explore investment opportunities and promote renewable energy solutions. These efforts are particularly relevant to supporting national energy resilience, reducing operational costs for businesses, encouraging innovation and creating new opportunities for local enterprises.

Minister Desaubin is accompanied by Mr Tony Imaduwa, Principal Secretary for Climate Affairs and Energy, and Ms Betty-May Bibi, Executive Director in the Office of the Minister for Industry and Enterprise.

Solar investment and agriculture lead Seychelles’ address at ISA Assembly

by K. Doku 

Financing solar projects and putting the technology to work in agriculture are among the priorities Seychelles has highlighted at the Ninth International Solar Alliance (ISA) Assembly in India.Minister for Industry and Enterprise Geralda Desaubin is representing the country at the meeting, which runs from 2 to 5 November in New Delhi. The gathering brings together member countries and energy stakeholders to discuss how to expand solar power and attract the investment needed to support it.

stories.title: Western Indian Ocean Conservation Trust Fund Proposed
stories.description: In a Project Syndicate article published on 23 October 2026, Seychelles’ Minister for Environment, Climate, Energy and Natural Resources (Marie-May Jeremie) calls for stronger regional cooperation and reliable, long-term conservation financing, including a proposed Western Indian Ocean Regional Conservation Trust Fund. The article advocates a region-led approach to protecting shared marine ecosystems.

publications.text:
🌊 Can regional cooperation secure the future of the Western Indian Ocean?

As countries marked 40 years of cooperation through the Nairobi Convention at COP12, the focus must move from commitments to lasting action.

In this Project Syndicate article, Seychelles’ Minister for Environment, Climate, Energy and Natural Resources, Marie-May Jeremie, who also serves as the President (WIOMSA - Western Indian Ocean Marine Science Association) highlights the need for stronger regional cooperation and reliable, long-term conservation financing, including a proposed Western Indian Ocean Regional Conservation Trust Fund. 

Building on progress already made by countries such as Seychelles, she calls for a region-led approach to protecting shared marine ecosystems for generations to come.
