stories.title: Seychelles Welcomes Russia–Africa Summit Outcomes
stories.description: In an interview published on 2 November 2026, Seychelles' foreign minister (Barry Faure) said Seychelles was satisfied with the outcomes of the Third Russia–Africa Summit in Moscow (Russia). He said adopted documents reflected Seychelles' priorities and welcomed the Russia–Africa Partnership Forum Action Plan for 2027–2029; he also said Seychelles' proposed Russia–Africa Climate Resilience Mechanism had been under discussion with Russian partners since December 2025.

publications.text:
🇷🇺🌍 SOMMET RUSSIE–AFRIQUE : À MOSCOU, VLADIMIR POUTINE DESSINE LES CONTOURS D’UN NOUVEL ORDRE MONDIAL

Moscou, 28 octobre 2026 - Derrière les discours sur la multipolarité, le troisième sommet Russie–Afrique révèle une ambition beaucoup plus vaste : réorganiser les relations économiques, financières, industrielles et diplomatiques entre Moscou et un continent africain qui entend désormais peser davantage sur les affaires du monde.

Et les annonces se multiplient.

Réunissant des délégations annoncées de 48 des 54 États africains, dont 22 représentés par leurs chefs d’État, le sommet est coprésidé par Vladimir Poutine et Évariste Ndayishimiye, président du Burundi et président en exercice de l’Union africaine.

Environ 4 000 représentants des milieux économiques russes et africains ont été invités au forum qui accompagne cette rencontre.

Le message politique est sans ambiguïté.

« Le monde multipolaire devient une réalité. Cette tendance est objective et irréversible », affirme Vladimir Poutine.

Le président russe estime que l’époque où un groupe restreint de puissances décidait du destin de continents entiers touche à sa fin. Il accuse certains pays occidentaux de perpétuer des mécanismes de dépendance économique hérités de la colonisation, notamment par l'endettement, les sanctions unilatérales et les politiques commerciales coercitives.

Selon les chiffres avancés par Poutine, les BRICS représentent désormais plus de 40 % de la production économique mondiale, contre moins de 30 % pour le G7. Cette comparaison repose sur une lecture de l'économie mondiale en parité de pouvoir d'achat, et non sur le PIB nominal.

Mais au-delà de cette confrontation des visions internationales, c'est un programme de coopération extrêmement concret que Moscou expose.

🔹 SOUVERAINETÉ FINANCIÈRE : RÉDUIRE LA DÉPENDANCE AU DOLLAR

Vladimir Poutine appelle les pays africains à développer leurs règlements commerciaux en monnaies nationales et à construire des systèmes de paiement moins dépendants des infrastructures financières occidentales.

Il demande également une réforme du FMI et de la Banque mondiale afin d'accorder davantage de poids aux économies émergentes et aux États africains.

La Russie met en avant ses programmes de conversion de dettes en financements destinés à des projets nationaux de développement.

L'objectif affiché : permettre aux pays africains de disposer d'une plus grande autonomie dans leurs choix économiques.

🔹 COMMERCE : UN OBJECTIF DE 50 MILLIARDS DE DOLLARS

Les échanges commerciaux entre la Russie et l'Afrique ont dépassé 27 milliards de dollars en 2025, contre environ 16,8 milliards en 2019.

Poutine estime qu'ils pourraient franchir prochainement le seuil des 50 milliards de dollars.

Une ambition considérable, même si le commerce russo-africain demeure encore très inférieur aux volumes enregistrés par la Chine et l'Union européenne avec le continent.

Moscou souhaite développer les investissements industriels, les chaînes logistiques, les infrastructures portuaires, routières et ferroviaires ainsi que les relations commerciales directes.

🔹 SÉCURITÉ ALIMENTAIRE : LA RUSSIE RENFORCE SON RÔLE DE FOURNISSEUR

Sur les neuf premiers mois de 2026, la Russie a exporté environ 13 millions de tonnes de céréales vers les pays africains, selon les chiffres communiqués par Moscou.

Plus de 40 pays du continent reçoivent des céréales ou des engrais russes.

Les exportations agricoles russes vers l'Afrique dépassent même 13,9 millions de tonnes sur la période, selon le centre fédéral Agroexport.

Poutine annonce vouloir élargir encore la géographie de ces approvisionnements et présente la Russie comme un acteur majeur de la sécurité alimentaire africaine.

🔹 ÉNERGIE ET RESSOURCES MINIÈRES : INDUSTRIALISER DAVANTAGE SUR PLACE

Moscou met en avant un portefeuille de plus de 30 projets énergétiques, à différents stades de développement, dans 16 pays africains.

Pétrole, gaz, électricité, nucléaire civil et infrastructures énergétiques figurent parmi les priorités.

Le groupe Rosatom poursuit notamment ses discussions avec plusieurs États africains sur le développement de l'énergie nucléaire.

La Russie propose également des coopérations dans la cartographie géologique, l'analyse des minerais et la formation de spécialistes africains.

Le message de Poutine est central : l'Afrique doit pouvoir exploiter ses ressources naturelles, mais aussi développer leur transformation industrielle sur son propre territoire.

Il assure que les entreprises russes entendent contribuer à cette création de valeur locale plutôt qu'à une simple extraction des matières premières.

🔹 TECHNOLOGIES ET INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE : LE TRANSFERT DE COMPÉTENCES COMME INSTRUMENT DIPLOMATIQUE

Poutine affirme que la Russie a consolidé sa souveraineté technologique et dispose, dans certains domaines, de compétences que ses concurrents chercheraient encore à rattraper.

Il cite notamment les technologies numériques et les modèles d'intelligence artificielle générative.

Moscou se déclare prête à partager des technologies et des savoir-faire avec ses partenaires africains.

Cybersécurité, infrastructures numériques, intelligence artificielle, énergie et formation scientifique sont présentées comme des domaines prioritaires.

Une déclaration spécifique sur la coopération dans les applications civiles de l'intelligence artificielle doit être soumise aux participants du sommet.

🔹 SANTÉ : PRODUIRE LES MÉDICAMENTS ET VACCINS EN AFRIQUE

Autre annonce importante : la volonté russe de localiser sur le continent africain certaines étapes de production de médicaments et de vaccins.

Moscou propose également des laboratoires, des centres de diagnostic et une coopération médicale renforcée.

Vladimir Poutine a évoqué la disponibilité des médecins russes pour contribuer à la lutte contre le choléra et Ebola.

La Russie annonce aussi la prolongation jusqu'en 2029 d'un programme d'assistance sanitaire destiné aux pays africains.

🔹 ÉDUCATION : FORMER LES FUTURES GÉNÉRATIONS AFRICAINES

Plus de 40 000 étudiants africains poursuivent actuellement leurs études en Russie, selon Moscou.

En parallèle, le groupe éducatif russe Synergie, avec le soutien d'Innopraktika, annonce l'ouverture de dix centres éducatifs en Afrique d'ici fin 2028.

Les premiers sont prévus au Maroc et au Nigeria.

En Tanzanie, un établissement de formation professionnelle doit ouvrir dès novembre 2026 pour préparer des soudeurs, électriciens, mécaniciens et autres techniciens.

L'enjeu dépasse l'éducation : il s'agit de créer des relations humaines, scientifiques et industrielles durables entre les deux espaces.

🔹 TRANSPORTS : OUVRIR DE NOUVELLES LIAISONS AÉRIENNES

Vladimir Poutine invite les compagnies aériennes africaines à établir des vols directs vers la Russie.

L'objectif est de soutenir le tourisme, les échanges d'affaires et la mobilité universitaire, tout en renforçant les liaisons entre les deux régions.

🔹 DES ACCORDS DÉJÀ SIGNÉS, D'AUTRES EN PRÉPARATION

En marge des rencontres, l'organisation russe Eurasia et des partenaires africains ont signé des accords et mémorandums de coopération avec des représentants de six pays : Mali, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Madagascar, Seychelles et Togo.

Ces textes concernent principalement l'éducation, la culture, les initiatives sociales et la coopération humanitaire. Il ne s'agit pas d'accords intergouvernementaux généraux.

D'autres engagements bilatéraux sont annoncés, notamment avec la République démocratique du Congo dans les domaines de la santé, de l'économie, des sciences et de la formation professionnelle.

Le sommet doit encore déboucher sur trois textes politiques majeurs :

▪️ Une déclaration finale commune.

▪️ Un plan d'action Russie–Afrique pour 2027-2029.

▪️ Une déclaration consacrée à la coopération sur l'intelligence artificielle.

Plus de 30 documents bilatéraux ou interinstitutionnels sont également attendus. Leur adoption et leur signature restent à confirmer à l'issue des travaux des 28 et 29 octobre.

🌍 AU-DELÀ DES DISCOURS, UN ENJEU GÉOPOLITIQUE MAJEUR

Ce qui se joue à Moscou n'est pas simplement une nouvelle étape du rapprochement entre la Russie et plusieurs capitales africaines.

C'est aussi la recherche d'un rééquilibrage des relations internationales.

Moscou tente de proposer une coopération couvrant simultanément la finance, l'alimentation, les infrastructures, les technologies, l'éducation et la santé.

Pour les États africains, l'intérêt réside notamment dans la possibilité de diversifier leurs partenaires, de négocier de nouvelles conditions de coopération et de renforcer leur autonomie de décision, sans nécessairement rompre leurs relations avec les pays occidentaux.

Il reste toutefois une distinction essentielle entre les déclarations, les mémorandums, les projets financés et les réalisations effectives. Le développement des échanges commerciaux et la mise en œuvre des engagements permettront de mesurer les résultats de ce sommet.

Une chose apparaît déjà clairement : la Russie entend faire de l'Afrique l'un des axes structurants de sa diplomatie et de sa stratégie économique de long terme.

Et les dirigeants africains entendent, de leur côté, ne plus être seulement les spectateurs des grandes transformations internationales.

C'est sans doute la dimension la plus significative de cette rencontre de Moscou.

**🇸🇨 Le chef de la diplomatie seychelloise **[**s’est félicité des résultats du troisième sommet Russie-Afrique**](https://afrinz.ru/fr/2026/11/le-chef-de-la-diplomatie-seychelloise-s-est-dit-satisfait-des-resultats-du-troisieme-sommet-russie-afrique/)

Les Seychelles sont satisfaites des résultats du troisième sommet Russie-Afrique, qui s’est tenu à Moscou, car les documents adoptés prennent en compte les intérêts essentiels de la République. C’est ce qu’a indiqué Barry Faure, ministre des Affaires étrangères et de la Diaspora des Seychelles, dans un entretien accordé à l’Agence de presse African Initiative.

« Les questions qui nous intéressent sont la durabilité environnementale, la préservation de la biodiversité, la gestion des ressources océaniques, la lutte contre le changement climatique, le commerce, le tourisme et la coopération économique. Nous avons constaté que toutes ces questions étaient dûment prises en compte dans les documents adoptés. Nous sommes également très heureux qu’un plan d’action pour la période 2027-2029 ait été adopté », a déclaré le ministre.

Barry Faure a également indiqué que les Seychelles avaient proposé la création d’un mécanisme russo-africain visant à renforcer la résilience climatique. Selon lui, cette initiative est en discussion avec les partenaires russes depuis décembre 2025.

« Ce mécanisme permettra de mettre à profit les connaissances et l’expérience de la Russie et des pays africains pour lutter contre les effets négatifs du changement climatique et atténuer les conséquences des catastrophes naturelles », a expliqué le chef de la diplomatie seychelloise.

Auparavant, Barry Faure avait indiqué dans un entretien que les Seychelles prévoyaient d’ouvrir une ambassade à Moscou au cours du premier trimestre 2027.

publications.title: In 1962, British newspaper editor Brendon Grimshaw purchased Moyenne Island,
publications.text:
In 1962, British newspaper editor Brendon Grimshaw purchased Moyenne Island, a tiny 9.9-hectare dot in the Seychelles, for just £8,000. 

At the time, the island had been abandoned for half a century, leaving it so densely overgrown with weeds and choked underbrush that falling coconuts literally never hit the ground. 

Alongside a local partner named René Antoine Lafortune, Grimshaw spent the next several decades clearing invasive brush by hand, constructing 5 kilometers of nature paths, and planting over 16,000 native trees, including mahogany, mango, and endemic palms.  

Their tireless efforts completely revived the local ecosystem. Native birds flocked back to the island, and Grimshaw successfully introduced and bred a thriving population of over 120 Aldabra giant tortoises, protecting them from regional extinction. 

As the Seychelles exploded into a luxury tourism hotspot, developers fiercely targeted Moyenne, offering Grimshaw up to $54 million to buy the property for a high-end resort. 

He steadfastly refused, famously asking investors where the birds would nest and where the tortoises would live. 

Instead of cashing out, Grimshaw worked with the Seychelles' Ministry of Environment to officially declare Moyenne Island a protected national park in 2009. 

Today, it stands as the smallest national park in the world, managed by a foundation that limits visitors to 50 at a time to honor Grimshaw’s lifelong vision of untouched tranquility.  

#DidYouKnow #facts #fyp

In 1962, a British journalist bought a tiny, abandoned island in the Indian Ocean for just £8,000.

What he did with it over the next 40 years was extraordinary.

Brendon Grimshaw had been working as a newspaper editor in East Africa when he discovered Moyenne Island, a small patch of land in the Seychelles.

The island had been largely abandoned for decades. Its vegetation was so overgrown that parts of it were almost impossible to walk through.

But Grimshaw saw something worth saving.

He eventually moved there and began an ambitious restoration project with a young Seychellois man named René Antoine Lafortune.

Together, they cleared invasive growth, planted approximately 16,000 trees by hand and created nearly three miles of nature trails.

They also introduced giant tortoises, helping establish a thriving population of the remarkable animals.

Over the years, birds returned, vegetation flourished and the neglected island gradually became a wildlife sanctuary.

As tourism expanded across the Seychelles, Grimshaw reportedly received offers worth millions from people interested in developing the island.

He refused to sell.

Instead, he spent years working toward legal protection for Moyenne.

In 2009, the island was officially designated a national park, securing the future of the place he and Lafortune had spent decades restoring.

Lafortune died in 2007, and Grimshaw followed in 2012 at the age of 87.

Today, Moyenne remains protected, with its forests, walking trails and giant tortoises still welcoming visitors.

He bought an island for £8,000 and left behind a national park. 💛

In 1962, British journalist Brendon Grimshaw purchased Moyenne Island in the Seychelles for £8,000. At the time, the small island was largely abandoned, but Grimshaw saw its potential to become something extraordinary—a thriving natural sanctuary.

With the help of his friend René Lafortune, Grimshaw devoted decades to restoring the island’s ecosystem. Together, they planted approximately 16,000 trees, created walking trails, encouraged native plant life to flourish, and helped bring wildlife back to the island. Giant Aldabra tortoises became one of its most remarkable attractions, while birds and lush vegetation transformed the once-neglected landscape.

His mission was about conservation, not profit. As Moyenne Island attracted interest from developers, Grimshaw reportedly turned down offers of up to $50 million rather than allow the island to be transformed into an exclusive commercial development.

His dedication helped secure the island’s future. Moyenne was designated a national park in 2008, with the formal designation reported in 2009, helping protect its natural environment for future generations.

Today, Moyenne Island stands as a powerful example of how patience, hard work, and a commitment to nature can transform an entire ecosystem. Grimshaw’s story reminds us that protecting the natural world can be far more valuable than accepting even the biggest financial offer.

One person, 16,000 trees, and a legacy that continues to inspire conservation.

What would you do if you had the chance to protect a piece of nature like this?

Sources:  BBC Travel — Moyenne Island: The World's Smallest National Park

POLICE STATEMENT (URGENT APPEAL)

The Seychelles Police are issuing an urgent appeal to the public, particularly families, urging anyone who has a missing family member to report the matter to the Police immediately.

The appeal follows an official report received by the Police late yesterday afternoon concerning a man who was riding a jet ski in the waters off Anse Soleil, Baie Lazare. The individual reportedly spotted what appeared to be the body of a man in the deeper waters.

According to the information provided, the person believed to be in the water was wearing a black wetsuit and had short hair.

Following the report, the Seychelles Coast Guard responded to provide assistance. This morning, the Marine Police launched a search operation in the waters stretching from Baie Lazare to Anse Boileau to verify the information received. However, no body has been located so far.

The Police confirm that, as of now, no official missing-person report has been received.

Chief Justice Rony Govinden has resigned. According to a press release from State House, he submitted his resignation letter to the Head of State in accordance with Article 131(1) (c) of the Constitution.

President Herminie acknowledges the Chief Justice's service to the Judiciary and the country and expresses his appreciation for his contribution to the administration of justice, states the press release. 

In accordance with the constitutional provisions governing the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice, the Constitutional Appointments Authority (CAA) will submit to the President the names of eligible Puisne Judges for consideration. 

The President will thereafter appoint an Acting Chief Justice to ensure continuity in the administration of justice, pending the appointment of a substantive Chief Justice.

The President has reaffirmed his commitment to upholding the independence of the Judiciary, the rule of law and the constitutional principles governing the administration of justice in Seychelles.

(Source: Office of the President)

Why would a Chief Justice resign at 55?

Chief justices do not walk away from the highest judicial office lightly. When they do, the reasons are usually compelling: ill health, age, exhaustion, the pursuit of other opportunities, controversy over judicial decisions, political considerations or questions surrounding their conduct.

So why has Seychelles’ Chief Justice, Ronny Govinden, resigned at the relatively young age of 55?

State House announced his resignation earlier today. President Patrick Herminie thanked him for his service since November 2020, but there appeared to be no public indication of an attempt to persuade him to reconsider.

The departure comes barely a week after the retirement of Court of Appeal President Justice Antony Fernando, leaving two significant leadership vacancies at the top of the judicial branch.

No reason has been given for Justice Govinden’s sudden departure. Yet, viewed against the political developments since the United Seychelles administration took office in October 2025, his resignation raises wider questions.

He is the latest in a succession of senior public officials to leave their positions, including Central Bank Governor Caroline Abel, Financial Intelligence Unit head Richard Rampal, Financial Services Authority chief executive Randolf Samson, Attorney-General Vinsent Perera, Registrar-General Wendy Zialor, Police Commissioner Ted Barbé and Seychelles Intelligence Services head Benediste Hoareau.

Governments routinely make senior appointments following a change of administration. But the scale and breadth of these departures invite a more uncomfortable question: is this merely institutional renewal, or is something deeper unfolding?

The concern is whether Seychelles is gradually moving towards a system of political patronage, where loyalty matters more than institutional independence, or whether the country is witnessing the consolidation of state power in the hands of a privileged few.

Neither conclusion should be reached without evidence. But the accumulation of departures, particularly within institutions meant to safeguard public accountability and the rule of law, deserves scrutiny.

In a democracy, institutions must be stronger than the individuals who occupy them.

Time will tell.

publications.text:
President Herminie Receives Resignation of Chief Justice Rony Govinden

The Office of the President said on Friday that President Dr Patrick Herminie has received the resignation of the Chief Justice of the Republic of Seychelles, Mr Rony Govinden.

The post President Herminie Receives Resignation of Chief Justice Rony Govinden appeared first on The Seychelles Times.

Chief Justice Rony Govinden has resigned with years still left on his term. The President accepted it without hesitation. 

The presidency of the Court of Appeal has stood empty for months. Two of the highest judicial offices in the country are now open at the same time, and the government that holds the presidency is already moving to shape who fills them.

The Constitution created the Constitutional Appointments Authority so that no single president could hand-pick the judges who will sit over him, his ministers, and his party. Two members are appointed by the President, two by the opposition, and they select the chair. That body is supposed to stand between the executive and the bench. The President has now taken that same Authority to the Constitutional Court. He is unhappy with the nominations coming forward. So the filter is being challenged, and the vacancies are waiting.

This is not a technical disagreement. It is a political project. The same administration that already rewrote the rules around the national broadcaster is now testing the rules around the courts. An early resignation is accepted. A senior vacancy is left open. The independent body that must propose the next names is hauled into court. The pattern is deliberate. When the people who recommend judges can be pressured or replaced, the next Chief Justice and the next President of the Court of Appeal can be chosen for reliability rather than independence.

In 1977 the country learned what concentrated power looks like. Force was used then. Today the methods are quieter, accepted resignations, prolonged vacancies, and litigation aimed at the institutions the Constitution built to restrain the executive. 

The Vice President and the rest of this government are part of the same exercise. They speak the language of the Constitution while they work to remove the parts of it that limit them. Once the acting appointment is made and the full process runs under the new conditions, the higher courts can be staffed by people who understand who controls their future.

Ordinary Seychellois will feel the result. When you take a case against the state, against a connected businessman, or against a decision that harms your family, the judge who hears you will know the political climate that put him or her on the bench. That is how justice is quietly bent. Not always with open orders. Sometimes with the knowledge that independence has a cost.

This government won an election. It did not win the right to rewrite the rules that keep the courts separate from the party in power. The early departure of the Chief Justice, the empty post at the Court of Appeal, and the case against the CAA are not isolated events. They are steps. If they succeed, the next generation of judges will be appointed under different expectations than the ones the Constitution set out.

Watch the names that appear. Watch whether the CAA is left intact or reshaped. Watch whether the new judges are known for standing apart from government or known for standing close to it. 1977 showed what happens when institutions fall under one set of hands. The same warning applies when those hands belong to the people who now hold State House and decide the Constitution is only useful when it serves them.

OFFICIAL STATEMENT

The Office of the President wishes to inform the public that His Excellency President Dr Patrick Herminie has received the resignation of the Chief Justice of the Republic of Seychelles, Mr Rony Govinden.

The resignation was submitted in accordance with Article 131(1)(c) of the Constitution of the Republic of Seychelles.

The President acknowledges Mr Govinden’s service to the Judiciary and the Republic of Seychelles and expresses his appreciation for his contribution to the administration of justice.

In accordance with the Constitution, the Constitutional Appointments Authority (CAA) will submit the names of eligible Puisne Judges to the President for consideration for appointment as Acting Chief Justice.

The President will subsequently appoint an Acting Chief Justice to ensure continuity in the administration of justice pending the appointment of a substantive Chief Justice.

The President reaffirms his commitment to safeguarding the independence of the Judiciary, upholding the rule of law and respecting the constitutional principles that underpin the administration of justice in Seychelles.

THE LIGHTHOUSE DOESN'T BELONG TO THE KEEPER
OracleMaster  Reflection :

On 6 November 2026, the Office of the President announced the resignation of Chief Justice Rony Govinden. A chapter has closed at the highest level of Seychelles' judiciary.

But the question isn't simply who comes next. The more important question is:

What do we want justice to look like moving forward?

THE LIGHTHOUSE PRINCIPLE

A lighthouse doesn't exist to honour its keeper. It exists so that every ship can trust the light it provides.

When a lighthouse keeper steps down, a wise harbour doesn't simply hand over the keys to the next person. It inspects the lamp, cleans the glass and asks whether the light remains trustworthy.

Chief Justice Govinden's resignation presents Seychelles with precisely that opportunity.

The strength of a judiciary isn't measured by the names displayed on its doors, but by the confidence the public places in its independence, integrity and impartiality.

🌱 WHY THIS MOMENT IS AN OPPORTUNITY

✨ An opportunity to reset standards, not merely change personnel.

✨ An opportunity to strengthen the systems that safeguard fairness and accountability.

✨ A reminder that no individual officeholder is greater than the institution they serve.

A resignation should not become a revolving door. Mr Govinden's departure could instead become a doorway to institutional renewal.

 THE CORE MESSAGE

1. Transparency over assumptions.

Concerns raised over the years deserve independent scrutiny. They should neither be buried nor presented as established facts without proper investigation.

2. Institutions over individuals.

There has been public discussion about whether Mr Govinden might seek another judicial appointment, such as Justice of Appeal. Any such appointment should be examined against the principles of public confidence, institutional integrity and judicial independence.

3. Impartiality must not only exist; it must be seen.

Even where no wrongdoing has been established, the justice system must maintain public confidence. Potential conflicts of interest and even the appearance of undue influence must be carefully addressed.

4. Accountability applies to everyone.

Oversight bodies and the Constitutional Appointments Authority must be prepared to face the same level of scrutiny they are expected to apply to others.

THE VISION

Imagine a Seychelles where every judicial appointment is open to scrutiny, where oversight institutions act with courage and independence, and where citizens can proudly say:

"Our courts belong to the people."

This is not about condemning anyone without evidence. It is about demanding transparency, independent review and the highest standards of public accountability.

The departure of a Chief Justice should mark the beginning of a new chapter, not simply the recycling of leadership while legitimate questions remain unanswered.

That's not a dream. That's a decision.

publications.text:
SRC AND THE DEPARTMENT OF BLUE ECONOMY FORMALISE COOPERATION THROUGH SIGNING OF A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING .

The Seychelles Revenue Commission and the Department of Blue Economy - Seychelles (DBE) have formalized their cooperation through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), establishing a framework for collaboration in areas of mutual interest, including information exchange, regulatory development and domestic revenue mobilization.

The MoU signed at the Department of Blue Economy on 10th November 2026 by the Principal Secretary of the Department of Blue Economy, Ms. Veronique Nibourette and the Acting Commissioner General of the Seychelles Revenue Commission, Mr. Fred Morel,  provides for the exchange of information and seeks to support the development and implementation of relevant frameworks for the Blue Economy, while strengthening cooperation in areas that contribute to domestic revenue mobilization.

Other areas of cooperation include joint awareness-raising initiatives, capacity-building activities in areas of specialized expertise and collaboration on matters of mutual interest.

STRENGTHENING DATA-DRIVEN DECISION-MAKING FOR SEYCHELLES’ BLUE ECONOMY

The Department of the Blue Economy, the Registration Division and the Seychelles Revenue Commission (SRC) today strengthened inter-institutional cooperation through two MOUs
 aimed at improving the collection, exchange and analysis of data to support the development of Seychelles’ Blue Economy.

The MoU was signed by the Principal Secretary for the Blue Economy, Ms. Veronique Nibourette, the Commissioner General of the Seychelles Revenue Commission, Mr.
Fred Morel, and the Registrar General, Mr. Suleiman Athanasius. Also present was the Secretary of State for Fisheries and Blue Economy, Mr. Alain de Comarmond.

The collaboration seeks to enhance the availability, quality and use of administrative and transactional data to support:

-Evidence-based policymaking: Strengthening the use of reliable data for policy formulation, planning and decision-making.
- Statistical analysis and forecasting: Improving the ability to analyse trends and support informed projections within thhe Blue Economy sector. 
- Improved data systems: Promoting better data collection, classifications, standards and statistical methodologies.
- Technical cooperation and capacity-building: Encouraging the exchange of expertise and institutional knowledge.

Through this partnership, the three institutions aim to share,  strengthen and improve the availability of information needed to guide the sustainable growth and development of Seychelles’ Blue Economy.

All information sharing will remain subject to applicable legislation, confidentiality requirements and appropriate data protection and information-security safeguards.

Better data. Stronger collaboration. More informed decisions for a sustainable Blue Economy.

#BlueEconomy #Seychelles #DataDrivenDecisionMaking #InstitutionalCollaboration #SustainableDevelopment

stories.title: James Mancham Overthrown as Seychelles President
stories.description: The publication states that James Mancham, Seychelles’ first president, was overthrown by France-Albert René in 1977. It gives no more precise date or specific location.

publications.text:
🌍 On June 5 1977 France-Albert René overthrew Seychelles president James Mancham in a coup while Mancham was attending a Commonwealth Heads of Government meeting in London.

The coup was largely bloodless. René declared a one-party state under the Seychelles People's Progressive Front and governed for 27 years.

René's governance record includes real development achievements Seychelles maintained relatively high living standards by regional comparison during his time in power. It also included suppression of political opposition, exile of Mancham and others, and an attempted counter-coup in 1981 involving mercenaries that added further instability.

Multiparty democracy was restored in 1993 under international pressure. Mancham returned from exile the same year. René continued governing through democratic elections until retiring in 2004.

Worth holding honestly. René is a complex figure whose record includes genuine governance achievements alongside documented suppression of political rights. The small island context Seychelles has a population of approximately 100,000 shapes both the intimacy of the political environment and the scale of what governance meant there.

Drop a comment if Seychelles political history deserves more attention.

And follow INSIDE AFRICA for more. 🌍

(OAU) WAS FOUNDED ON 25 MAY 1963 IN ADDIS ABABA, ETHIOPIA. IT ENDED ON 9 JULY 2002 AND BECAME THE AFRICAN UNION. DURING THOSE 39 YEARS, AFRICA SAW KINGS, FREEDOM FIGHTERS, SOLDIERS, DICTATORS AND DEMOCRATS. THIS IS THE STORY OF EVERY ONE OF THEM, COUNTRY BY COUNTRY, WHEN THEY ENTERED AND HOW THEY ENDED

ALGERIA
*AHMED BEN BELLA - 1962 TO 1965*
He was the first President of independent Algeria. He was overthrown by his own army chief Houari Boumediene in a bloodless coup in 1965. He was kept under house arrest for 14 years and died in 2012.
*HOUARI BOUMEDIENE - 1965 TO 1978*
He took power by coup. He ruled with an iron hand and built Algeria into a strong socialist state. He died in office in 1978 of a rare blood disease.
*CHADLI BENDJEDID - 1979 TO 1992*
He became President after Boumediene. He tried to open Algeria to democracy but the army forced him to resign in 1992 when Islamists were about to win elections. He died in 2012.
*MOHAMED BOUDIAF - JANUARY 1992 TO JUNE 1992*
He was brought back from exile to lead. He was assassinated on live television in June 1992.
*ALI KAFI - 1992 TO 1994*
He was appointed by the army. He stepped down and was replaced.
*LIAMINE ZEROUAL - 1994 TO 1999*
A general who became President. He resigned in 1999 and retired from politics.
*ABDELAZIZ BOUTEFLIKA - 1999 TO 2019*
He ruled for 20 years. He was forced to resign in 2019 after mass protests against his fifth term. He died in 2021.

ANGOLA
*AGOSTINHO NETO - 1975 TO 1979*
First President after independence from Portugal. He led the country into civil war. He died in office in Moscow in 1979 during cancer treatment.
*JOSE EDUARDO DOS SANTOS - 1979 TO 2017*
He ruled for 38 years, one of the longest in Africa. He stepped down voluntarily in 2017 and handed over to Joao Lourenco. He died in Spain in 2022.

BENIN
*HUBERT MAGA - 1960 TO 1963, 1970 TO 1972*
He was overthrown twice by the military.

He was overthrown by a coup.
*SOUROU-MIGAN APITHY - 1964 TO 1965*
He was overthrown by the army.
*JUSTIN AHOMADEGBE-TOMETIN - 1965 TO 1965*
He ruled for a few months before another coup.
*TAHIRU CONGACOU - 1965 TO 1965*
He was interim President for a few weeks.
*CHRISTOPHE SOGLO AGAIN - 1965 TO 1967*
He was overthrown again.
*ALPHONSE ALLEY - 1967 TO 1968*
Military ruler who handed over.
*EMILE DERLIN ZINSOU - 1968 TO 1969*
He was overthrown by the army.
*PAUL-EMILE DE SOUZA - 1969 TO 1970*
Military ruler.
*HUBERT MAGA, JUSTIN AHOMADEGBE AND SOUROU APITHY - 1970 TO 1972 - PRESIDENTIAL COUNCIL*
They ruled together in rotation. The army overthrew them in 1972.
*MATHIEU KEREKOU - 1972 TO 1991, 1996 TO 2006*
He took power by coup in 1972 and became a Marxist dictator. He lost elections in 1991 and left peacefully. He returned by winning elections in 1996 and left in 2006 after term limits. He died in 2015.
*NICEphORE SOGLO - 1991 TO 1996*
He won the first democratic election. He lost to Kerekou in 1996 and left peacefully.

Military ruler. He was overthrown in 1980.

Military ruler. He was overthrown in 1982.

Military ruler. He was overthrown by Thomas Sankara in 1983.

He ruled for 27 years. He was forced to resign and flee to Ivory Coast in 2014 after people rose against his attempt to stay longer.

Military ruler. He was overthrown by Buyoya in 1987.

stories.title: Seychelles First Lady Presents Four-Year Social Strategy
stories.description: Véronique Herminie presented a four-year social strategy at State House (Seychelles) on 23 October 2026, aimed at strengthening community initiatives. The programme prioritises education, women’s empowerment, health and the wellbeing of vulnerable people, with implementation expected to rely on mobilising resources and partners. The publication says funding, selected projects and results will show whether the strategy translates into concrete action.

publications.text:
Seychelles : Véronique Herminie dévoile une stratégie sociale sur quatre ans

Les femmes, les enfants et les personnes vulnérables au cœur des priorités.

La Première dame des Seychelles, Véronique Herminie, a présenté le 23 octobre 2026, à State House, une stratégie sociale sur quatre ans visant à renforcer les initiatives communautaires.

Le programme met l’accent sur l’éducation, l’autonomisation des femmes, la santé et le bien-être des personnes vulnérables. Sa mise en œuvre reposera notamment sur la mobilisation de ressources et de partenaires.

Au-delà des annonces, le défi sera de traduire ces orientations en actions concrètes et mesurables. Les financements mobilisés, les projets retenus et les résultats obtenus permettront d’évaluer l’efficacité de cette stratégie.

L’enjeu : améliorer durablement les conditions de vie des populations les plus vulnérables.

stories.description: At the World Governments Summit, Wavel Ramkalawan of Seychelles, Gaston Browne of Antigua and Barbuda, and Faisal Naseem of the Maldives discuss climate risks facing small island nations, including rising temperatures, sea-level rise, extreme weather and threats to ocean resources. The publication dated 31 October 2026 says they called for stronger international emissions commitments to keep global warming within 1.5°C; it does not specify when the discussion took place.

publications.title: Why the World Is Falling Short on Climate Action | Hon. Wavel Ramkalawan - World Governments Summit
publications.text:
What happens to small island nations when climate change becomes a question of survival?

The Hon. Gaston Browne, Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda, and The Hon. Wavel Ramkalawan, Former President of Seychelles, discuss the climate challenges facing Small Island Developing States (SIDS) and the need for stronger international action on climate finance, emissions and green energy.

The conversation explores the gap between climate commitments and the realities faced by vulnerable countries. Ramkalawan highlights the disproportionate impact of climate change on Africa and small island nations, including rising coastal erosion and the threat to the survival of island communities. Browne discusses the need for greater climate finance, investment in green energy technologies and support for developing countries that contribute relatively little to global emissions.

They also examine the role of climate finance, green energy, climate reparations, the polluter-pays principle and technology transfer in accelerating the transition to cleaner energy, particularly across developing countries and Small Island Developing States.

In this conversation:
- Climate change and Small Island Developing States
- Climate finance for developing countries
- The $100 billion climate finance commitment
- Climate commitments and international action
- The impact of climate change on island nations
- Coastal erosion and rising climate risks
- Africa’s share of global emissions
- Green energy and clean technology
- Making green technologies more affordable
- Climate reparations and financial support
- The polluter-pays principle
- Climate justice and vulnerable nations
- Fossil fuel vehicles and developing countries
- Technology transfer for developing economies
- The future of global climate cooperation

The conversation highlights why climate change must remain part of discussions around the changing global order and why financing, technology and international cooperation are critical for countries on the front lines of climate change.

Watch the full conversation to hear how Antigua and Barbuda and Seychelles are calling for stronger global action on climate change, climate finance and the survival of vulnerable nations.

publications.title: Our Planet Is Getting Destroyed | Hon. Wavel Ramkalawan - World Governments Summit
publications.text:
Small island nations are on the front lines of climate change but they argue they did the least to cause it.

At the World Governments Summit, The Hon. Wavel Ramkalawan, President of Seychelles; The Hon. Gaston Browne, Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda; and H.E. Faisal Naseem, Vice President of Maldives discuss the growing climate risks facing island nations and the urgent need for global action.

The leaders highlight the disproportionate impact of rising temperatures, sea-level rise, extreme weather, and threats to ocean resources. They also call for stronger international commitments to reduce emissions and keep global warming within 1.5°C.

For countries such as Seychelles, Antigua and Barbuda, and the Maldives, climate change is not a distant concern—it is increasingly tied to survival, food security, livelihoods, and the future of their communities.

The message from these frontline states is clear: what happens to small island nations today could be a warning of what lies ahead for the rest of the world.

stories.title: Seychelles Minister Calls for Safe Traditional Medicine Access
stories.description: A Facebook publication dated 20 October 2026 reports that Seychelles Health Minister Dr Marvin Fanny addressed a high-level forum in Beijing (China), bringing the perspective of Small Island Developing States. He called for greater access to medical expertise, research and training, and said traditional medicine should be supported by scientific evidence, proper regulation and patient safety; the address date is not specified.

publications.text:
As part of his engagements in Beijing, Minister of Health Dr Marvin Fanny held a bilateral meeting with Mr. Huang Luqi, Vice Commissioner of China's National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine (NATCM), the Government body responsible for overseeing and developing traditional Chinese medicine.

The Minister sought to reactivate cooperation between NATCM and Seychelles, with a focus on training, research and technical exchanges that can bring practical benefits to the country's healthcare system.

The Minister also raised the potential role of traditional Chinese medicine in complementing existing approaches to mental health and drug addiction, two pressing national challenges that the Government has made a priority, with an emphasis on exploring safe, evidence-based treatment options.

The Ministry is drawing on China’s experience to strengthen healthcare services and expand treatment options in Seychelles.

On the second day of his official visit to China, Minister of Health, Dr Marvin Fanny, addressed the Government Forum of the World Conference on Traditional Medicine 2026 in Beijing.

The Forum brings together government representatives, health professionals and researchers to examine how traditional medicine can be safely and effectively integrated into modern healthcare, while strengthening international cooperation.

Minister Fanny outlined Seychelles' intention to take a more structured approach to traditional medicine, with greater emphasis on regulation, scientific research and the careful introduction of evidence-based treatments into public healthcare, particularly in pain management and rehabilitation.

At a separate high-level roundtable, the Minister highlighted Seychelles' medicinal plants and traditional remedies, calling for stronger research partnerships to explore their potential medical applications while safeguarding the country's biodiversity and traditional knowledge.

The Minister also stressed the importance of turning existing agreements into practical cooperation. Seychelles and China signed a Memorandum of Understanding on traditional medicine in September 2025, covering research, professional training, regulation and clinical cooperation.

For the Ministry of Health, the direction is clear: traditional medicine must be assessed not simply for its potential, but for the difference it can make to patient care, with scientific evidence, safety and long-term sustainability guiding its place in Seychelles' healthcare system.

To wrap up his participation in the World Conference on Traditional Medicine 2026 in Beijing, Minister of Health Dr Marvin Fanny addressed the High-Level Forum on Belt and Road Cooperation for Traditional Chinese Medicine Development.

In his address, Minister Fanny brought the perspective of Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to the discussion, stressing that smaller countries must not be left behind as traditional medicine gains greater international recognition.
He called for greater access to medical expertise, research and training, while emphasising that traditional medicine must be supported by scientific evidence, proper regulation and patient safety.

Minister Fanny was accompanied by Mr Hervé Pool, Chargé d’Affaires a.i. at the Embassy of Seychelles in China; Mr Marc Ernesta, Pharmacist at the Ministry of Health; and Mr Marthy Vidot, Personal Assistant to the Minister.

# 🇸🇨 SEYCHELLES PULSE

*Truth. Transparency. Accountability.*

## A PRESIDENT RETURNS WITH RENEWED STRENGTH: HERMINIE’S RECOVERY MARKS A MOMENT FOR LEADERSHIP, UNITY AND POLITICAL MATURITY

As President Patrick Herminie prepares to resume his presidential duties following his release from hospital, Seychelles Pulse extends its heartfelt wishes for continued good health, renewed strength and success as he begins another year of leadership.

His return to office should be welcomed as an opportunity to refocus the nation’s attention on the challenges facing Seychelles, the expectations of its people and the responsibilities that come with the highest office in the land.

**The President’s health is a human matter that should rise above political rivalry.**

Yet the period surrounding his illness has also raised uncomfortable questions about the state of political discourse in Seychelles. Reports and allegations of exaggerated claims, speculation and disturbing expressions of hostility circulating in political discussions have demonstrated how quickly a person’s health can become a weapon in the battle for public opinion.

If political activists or leaders associated with LDS spread unverified claims about the seriousness of the President’s condition, such conduct deserves firm criticism. And if individuals genuinely wished death upon a sitting President, that behaviour would be indefensible, regardless of political affiliation.

**Political opposition is a democratic right. Dehumanisation is not.**

LDS must understand that challenging President Herminie’s policies, scrutinising his decisions and holding his administration accountable are legitimate democratic responsibilities. But political competition loses its moral credibility when personal suffering becomes an opportunity for mockery, speculation or celebration.

No party that claims to stand for democratic values should tolerate such conduct among its supporters. Equally, allegations against particular individuals must be supported by evidence rather than used to condemn every member or supporter of an entire political movement.

As President Herminie enters another year of his mandate, his strongest political response will not be retaliation against his opponents. It will be effective leadership, transparent governance, tangible improvements in the lives of Seychellois citizens and a willingness to answer difficult questions.

For United Seychelles and its supporters, the President’s return provides an opportunity to demonstrate confidence in their leadership while remaining focused on the national priorities of the people. Political endorsement, however, must ultimately be earned through results, accountability and the fulfilment of promises.

### SEYCHELLES PULSE: PRINCIPLES BEFORE POLITICS

At Seychelles Pulse, our position is clear: **Truth. Transparency. Accountability.**

We believe that political journalism must defend human dignity, challenge misinformation and scrutinise those in power without abandoning fairness. We will not celebrate illness, encourage hatred or confuse political criticism with personal cruelty.

We wish President Patrick Herminie continued recovery, good health and the strength to carry out his responsibilities with wisdom and determination.

As he returns to his duties, may his administration demonstrate that the best answer to political hostility is responsible leadership, and that the greatest political achievement is not defeating an opponent through humiliation, but earning the trust of the nation through service.

**Seychelles deserves a politics of ideas, integrity and humanity not one built on rumours, cruelty and wishes of misfortune.**

*SEYCHELLES PULSE 🇸🇨*
*Truth. Transparency. Accountability.*
*Follow the money. Ask the questions. Keep Seychelles informed.*

“I am fit to resume duty tomorrow. I will be President until 2030.” — President Herminie

President of the Republic Dr Patrick Herminie resumes official duties tomorrow, Wednesday 28 October, following a period of medical leave during which he was admitted to the Seychelles Hospital.

Speaking to the State House Press Office, the President described the attention around his health as “a storm in a teacup.”

He said the Government is delivering across all sectors, and that some opponents, with little else to challenge, have exaggerated his illness, much of it through anonymous and fake social media profiles.

The President noted that most Seychellois understand illness is part of being human. Wishing harm on others, he said, goes against the values we learnt from our elders. He expressed regret that some individuals had used his illness for political ends, with some going as far as wishing for his death to trigger fresh elections.

The President also explained what the Constitution provides should a sitting President die in office.

He thanked everyone who kept him in their thoughts and prayers.

(Source: State House)

Seychelles moves to strengthen national framework for radiation safety and nuclear security

by H. Siu
 
Seychelles is strengthening its national framework for radiation safety and nuclear security through a stakeholder consultation workshop to improve regulatory oversight, identify challenges, and clarify responsibilities for institutions involved in the use and control of radioactive materials.

For full context and detailed reporting, read the complete article in today’s edition. Subscribe by calling +248 4290999 or email us at sales@today.sc

The Ministry of Employment and Resource Planning is intensifying efforts to enhance Seychelles' national framework for radiation safety and nuclear security by developing a comprehensive National Policy and Strategy. A team of four experts from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is currently in the country to conduct a workshop and hold consultations with representatives from ministries, government departments, regulatory authorities, and other relevant organisations involved in these areas.

During this one-week mission, the team is focusing on reviewing and strengthening legal, technical, and local administrative frameworks. Participants are evaluating the current national landscape for radiation safety and nuclear security in Seychelles, while clarifying their roles and responsibilities to foster better coordination and collaboration across the country.

To note, the Ministry of Employment and Human Resource Planning is the designated competent authority for radiation safety and nuclear security in Seychelles.

stories.title: Tropical Depression Forecast to Bring Heavy Rain to Seychelles
stories.description: The post reports that a system over Seychelles intensified into a tropical depression overnight and was located at 4.9°S, 53.9°E at 10:00 on 20 October 2026. An orange alert for heavy rain was in force for Mahé (Seychelles), Praslin (Seychelles), La Digue (Seychelles), Silhouette (Seychelles), Bird Island (Seychelles), Denis Island (Seychelles), the Amirantes (Seychelles), Alphonse (Seychelles) and Coëtivy (Seychelles); further intensification and naming as Agueda that afternoon were expected, with favorable conditions forecast for about 48 hours before gradual weakening.

publications.text:
[ 🌀DÉPRESSION TROPICALE 01🌀 ]

Bonjour,

🌀Le système évoluant au-dessus des Seychelles s’est intensifié en une dépression tropicale depuis la nuit dernière.⬆️

👉À 10 h ce matin, elle était localisée par par les points 4,9° Sud / 53,9° Est. La pression minimale est estimée à 1003 hPa, avec des rafales dépassant 75 km/h près du centre🌬. Le système se déplace vers l’ouest-sud-ouest à 9 km/h.🌊

🧏‍♂️Son intensification se poursuit, et un baptême sous le nom d’**AGUEDA** est prévue cet après-midi.✅️

🌀La dépression bénéficie encore d’environ 48 heures de conditions favorables à son évolution, après quoi elle devrait progressivement s’affaiblir🌫.

☝️Pendant cette période, elle devrait continuer à apporter d’importantes précipitations🌧 sur les îles des Seychelles, où une⚠️ alerte orange pour fortes pluies est en vigueur pour ⚠️Mahé, Praslin, La Digue, Silhouette, les îles Bird et Denis, les Amirantes, Alphonse et Coëtivy.🌩

☝️Le passage de cyclones🌀 sur les Seychelles est rare, mais possible. Le plus récent fut la 🌀tempête 01 de septembre 2002, qui avait causé d’importants dégâts sur les îles de Mahé et de Praslin❗️.🌧

Source : METEO FRANCE REUNION, SEYCHELLES BROADCASTING COORPERATION, MTOTEC, MCU

[ACTIVITÉ CYCLONIQUE]
Le 19/10/2026 à 8h30

👉 L'activité convective de la zone perturbée évoluant à proximité des Seychelles semble s'être renforcée au cours de la nuit dernière.
En l'absence de données satellites disponibles à cette heure, difficile d'affirmer, en revanche, que la cyclogenèse ait réellement démarré.

👉 Les modélisations continuent d'envisager un stade de dépression tropicale dans les prochaines 48h.
Le risque de formation de tempête à 72h est lui aussi en hausse sensible. AGUEDA n'est peut être pas si loin au final...

👉 Comme attendu, ce phénomène en gestation engendre des conditions perturbées sur les "îles intérieures" (Mahé, Praslin, La Digue...) des Seychelles.
Ainsi, depuis minuit, ces îles enregistrent des cumuls de pluie allant de 50 à 80 mm...et près de 300 mm sur la semaine. Localement, probablement sous orage, des rafales de vent frisant les 50 à 60 km/h sont également observés.

stories.title: Thirty Seychelles Staff Trained in Sea Turtle Monitoring
stories.description: A Facebook post published on 26 October 2026 reported that 30 staff members from MECENR and partner agencies recently took part in a one-day sea turtle monitoring and conservation training at Olympic House, Roche Caiman (Seychelles). Led by conservation biologist Dr Jeanne Mortimer, the training covered turtle identification, nesting activity, nest monitoring, data collection and tagging; the exact training date was not specified.

publications.text:
🐢 Strengthening Sea Turtle Conservation in Seychelles

Thirty staff members from MECENR and its partner agencies recently took part in a one-day training on sea turtle monitoring and conservation, led by Seychellois conservation biologist and internationally recognised sea turtle expert Dr Jeanne Mortimer.

Held at Olympic House, Roche Caiman, the training covered sea turtle identification, nesting activity, track recording, nest monitoring, data collection and the importance of turtle tagging.

With the hawksbill turtle nesting season underway, strengthening these skills is vital to improving monitoring, identifying threats such as poaching and protecting nesting beaches across Seychelles.

The training supports MECENR’s ongoing efforts to strengthen conservation and enforcement and ensure that sea turtles can continue to nest safely on our shores for generations to come. 🌊

stories.description: Seychelles launched its first National Action Plan on Women, Peace and Security for 2026–2031, according to the publication dated 8 October 2026. 7.  A controversy has erupted over the naming of the newly constructed East-West Vidyavihar bridge next to Vidyavihar station in Mumbai, ahead of its opening to traffic.

The Shiv Sena (UBT) recently put up a banner on the structure demanding that it be named after late actor Nana Patekar, days after BJP MLA Parag Shah sought to name it after Captain Smit Machchhar.

------ *MISHAPS*----------

1.  In Kota, Rajasthan — Eight Pilgrims Killed as Minibus Plunges into Drain
Eight pilgrims from Madhya Pradesh's Bhopal and Betul districts were killed and 16 injured when their minibus to the Khatu Shyamji temple veered off the Delhi–Mumbai Expressway and fell into a 15-foot-deep drain early on Saturday. Police suspect the driver dozed off.

2.  In Hyderabad, Telangana — Student Killed as Lighting Truss Collapses at Dandiya Night:  A 19-year-old engineering student was killed and around 15 others injured when an aluminium truss holding lights and speakers fell during a Dandiya night at MVSR Engineering College, Nadergul, on Saturday night. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy conveyed condolences.

3.  The death toll in the stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening rose to 19, most of them girls and children, with 25 injured, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said. He announced ₹25 lakh and a government job for each victim's family and ₹5 lakh for the injured; PM Narendra Modi announced a ₹2 lakh ex gratia, and police have detained 12 people, including puja organisers and volunteers, for questioning.
------------------------------------
    *DEFENCE News* 
------------------------------------
1.  Three ships of the Indian Navy’s First Training Squadron — INS Tir, INS Sujata and ICGS Sarathi — departed Victoria, Seychelles, on 15 October after a port call. The Defence Ministry said the engagement included professional training, capacity building and calls on Seychelles Defence Force Chief Maj Gen Michael Rosette.

2.  DRDO is developing a man-portable Electronic Intelligence (ELINT) system to detect, intercept and analyse signals from enemy radars, drones and other transmitters. Hyderabad's Defence Electronics Research Laboratory (DLRL) has issued a tender for the compact system, meant for frontline units in mountainous and remote areas.

3.  The Indian Army's Assam Regiment team won a gold medal at Exercise Cambrian Patrol 2026 in Wales, UK. Organised by the British Army since 1959, the demanding patrolling exercise is known as the 'Olympics of Military Patrolling'.

4.  India is developing an integrated tri-service defence logistics network to support the planned theatre commands. Led by the Department of Military Affairs and broadly modelled on the US framework, it aims to unify supply, maintenance and inventory management across the Army, Navy and Air Force.

5.  Dehradun-based start-up Picraft Technology validated its swarm drone technology in high-altitude trials at about 16,500 feet in Ladakh, demonstrating autonomous operations in low air density, strong winds and sub-zero temperatures.

6.  Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders laid the keel of the fifth Fast Patrol Vessel (Y-16505) and began production of the eighth, under its project to build 14 indigenous Fast Patrol Vessels for the Indian Coast Guard.
------------------------------------
✈ *INTERNATIONAL NEWS* 
------------------------------------
1.  US President Donald Trump waived key provisions of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, including threatened 100% tariffs on major buyers of Russian oil such as India, citing national interest. The waiver, issued a day before the law was to take effect, suspends but does not repeal the penalties.

2.  India told the UN that its Constitution guarantees peaceful assembly, citing a satirical youth movement, widely seen as the Cockroach Janta Party, as proof that young Indians can openly challenge the government. It rejected UN criticism of protest detentions as based on unverified claims.

stories.title: Ministers Meet La Digue (Seychelles) Residents on Transport Challenges
stories.description: Over 7–8 November 2026, Transport, Ports and Civil Aviation Minister Veronique Laporte visited La Digue (Seychelles) with a delegation, accompanied by Local Government and Inner Islands Minister Eveline Rose and an MNA for the island. The visit included a public meeting lasting more than three hours to discuss roads, bicycles—particularly motorbikes—and other transport, including buggies; the publication gives no specific decisions or outcomes.

publications.text:
ImNews | Seychelles Transport Minister Laporte Evaluates La Digue Infrastructure Projects

Seychelles Transport Minister Laporte assesses La Digue infrastructure, engages with residents on transport needs.....

Read the full story: https://t.co/WGoGtaNnnj

Minister Laporte Concludes La Digue Visit with Engagement at SPA Pier and Terminal

To conclude her official visit to La Digue, the Minister for Transport, Ports and Civil Aviation, Ms. Veronique Laporte, today visited the Seychelles Ports Authority (SPA) Pier and La Digue Terminal.
The visit provided an opportunity for the Minister to interact with some of the staff on duty, observe the working environment and gain a better understanding of their concerns, particularly regarding areas where improvements to the working conditions and facilities may be needed.

Discussions also touched on transport services on the island and matters relating to their operations.

The Minister confirmed that during her next visit to La Digue, expected before the end of the year in connection with the proclamation of roads and other road-related matters, she will also dedicate more time to meeting with SPA staff. This will provide an opportunity to follow up on the concerns and matters raised during today's visit, while also engaging with other staff members who were not on duty, to hear their views and better understand their needs.

Seychelles Ports Authority

Minister Laporte Visits La Digue to Assess Transport Projects and Engage with Residents

The Minister for Transport, Ports and Civil Aviation, Ms. Veronique Laporte, undertook an official visit to La Digue over the weekend, to assess ongoing infrastructure projects, identify areas requiring attention, discuss future development priorities and engage with residents on transport-related matters affecting the island.

As part of the visit, the Minister held a public meeting to discuss the way forward for transport on La Digue, taking into consideration the island's economic activities and the type of road infrastructure required to support its future development. The meeting provided residents with an opportunity to express their views and share their concerns on these matters. Minister Laporte also committed to returning to La Digue following the proclamation of public roads to further engage with residents on enforcement measures and the various rules and regulations that will govern the use of roads on the island.

She was accompanied by a delegation comprising the Principal Secretary for the Department of Land Transport, Ms. Sheryl Vengadasamy; the Principal Secretary for the Department of Ports and Civil Aviation, Mr. David Bianchi; Chief Technical Adviser at the Ministry, Mr. Elvis Octave; Chief Executive Officer of the Seychelles Land Transport Agency (SLTA), Mr. Parinda Herath; Chief Executive Officer of the Seychelles Ports Authority (SPA), Mr. Pierre Prosper; Deputy Chief Executive Officer of SLTA, Mr. Nicholas Hoareau; and Executive Director to the Minister, Ms. Vanessa Marie.

Minister Laporte was welcomed by the Honourable Member of the National Assembly (MNA) for La Digue, Mr. Rocky Uranie. The visit began with a meeting at the Department of Land Transport (DOLT) office on La Digue, where the delegation met with the Department's representative officer, Ms. Helda Evenor, to discuss operational matters, transport-related challenges and policy issues affecting the island.

The delegation subsequently visited several completed and ongoing infrastructure projects being implemented by SLTA. These included the drainage project near the school, recently resurfaced roads at Dan Mang and La Passe, as well as bridge repair works at Anse Sévère.

Particular attention was also given to several earth roads affected by flooding during the recent heavy rainfall. Maintenance works have commenced to restore these roads, including re-levelling and the application of coral fill to improve road conditions and accessibility.

The Minister also visited locations identified for future road improvement projects, including Pension Michel Road and Anse Gaulette, where works are scheduled to commence later this year and in 2027.

During the site visits and engagements, Minister Laporte and her delegation were joined by the Minister for Local Government and Inner Islands, Ms. Eveline Rose, together with officials from her Ministry.

The visit concluded with a public meeting at the La Digue Community Centre, attended by a sizeable number of residents. The meeting was chaired by the Minister for Transport, Ports and Civil Aviation and also attended by the Minister for Local Government and Inner Islands and the Honourable MNA for La Digue.

Presentations were delivered by SLTA and DOLT, outlining ongoing and planned infrastructure projects, transport policies and related initiatives. The meeting also provided residents with an opportunity to raise concerns, share their views and engage directly with the Ministers and officials on various transport-related matters affecting the island.

Jeg overvant også et par fobier💪🏻😀 Gummimaske over munn og nese (etter dårlig narkoseopplevelse som 4 åring) og det å ha hodet under vann. 🫣
Så nå tør jeg å 🤿 Stor seier!🥳

En fantastisk øy, og første av tre vi skal utforske😃🌴🐠

Annonce météo!
Oui je sais on en a marre de ces postes sur la météo mais là il est important de donner des informations.

Le temps que nous vivons en ce moment n'a rien a voir avec les dernières semaines où on avait un temps certes mitigé mais avec quand même de belles journées ensoleillée, accompagnées de passages nuageux et de pluies passagères certains jours. Il était quand meme possible de profiter des Seychelles car le soleil était bien présent 1 jour sur 2.

Là en ce moment depuis samedi, c'est différent, il y a une grosse dépression et un cyclone en formation pas loin des îles intérieures des Seychelles. Ceci est un phénomène exceptionnel, de tout temps il n'y a jamais eu de cyclone en formation si proche des îles intérieures des Seychelles (ni une tempête tropicale en octobre d'ailleurs). Alors ceci apporte une tempête tropicales (pluies abondantes, vent forts) qui va durer jusqu'à mercredi. Puis à partir de jeudi ça va se dissiper et le beau temps habituel d'octobre va normalement arriver dès vendredi, avec un beau temps et un océan calme prévu à partir de jeudi ou vendredi.

Pour les personnes présentes aux Seychelles, je suis vraiment désolé pour vous mais malheureusement c'est un phénomène exceptionnel, et ca tombe sur vous. Faites attention, il vaut mieux ne pas trop bouger pendant les prochains jours car il peut y avoir des pluies très abondantes (risque d'inondation) et des vents forts (donc risque accrue de chute d'arbres et de branches). 

Et pour ceux qui arrivent à partir de jeudi, ne vous faites pas de soucis car tout ceci sera derrière nous et le beau temps va revenir.

Bon courage pour les personnes qui sont ici, faites attention et pour les autres on a hâte de vous accueillir avec le beau temps d'ici la fin de la semaine 😊

Mauritius authorities appeal for relatives of man believed to be Seychellois

Authorities in Mauritius are appealing to relatives of a man believed to be from Seychelles to claim his body, which has remained in a hospital mortuary for 21 months.

The man, identified as 64-year-old Frank Jeffrey Marie, reportedly died in an accident on New Truck Road in Roche-Bois on 3 January 2025.

His body has remained at the SSRN Hospital mortuary since his death, with no relatives coming forward to claim it.

Several Mauritians have since taken to social media, suggesting that Marie was originally from Seychelles.

His last known address in Mauritius was on Balisage Street.

It remains unclear whether Mauritian authorities have contacted the Seychelles High Commission over the matter.

➡️ Depuis la nuit dernière, le système n°01-20262027 a présenté des signes nets d'organisation avec un renforcement de l'activité pluvio-orageuse accompagné d'une circulation dépressionnaire mieux définie. 

➡️ Estimé au stade de dépression tropicale en cours de nuit, le minimum dépressionnaire a évolué en tempête tropicale ce matin comme l'attestent des données de vents mesurées par satellite, reçues en fin de matinée.

➡️ Cette tempête à été baptisée AGUEDA peu après la mi-journée alors que son centre s'éloigne des îles principales des Seychelles (qui sont sorties de la zone pluvieuse principale associée à la tempête).

➡️ AGUEDA devrait encore influencer le temps sur certaines îles de l'archipel des Seychelles au cours des prochains jours. Aucune menace cyclonique n'est envisagée ni pour La Réunion ni pour Mayotte.

➡️ La formation précoce de AGUEDA (plus de 3 semaines avant la date médiane d'apparition de la première tempête tropicale) à proximité des Seychelles, apparaît comme un événement sortant de l'ordinaire. Elle a eu lieu à relativement faible distance de l'équateur (un peu plus de 400 km) et son positionnement est très à l'ouest sur le bassin pour un phénomène de début de saison. 

➡️ Il faut remonter à début septembre 2002 pour voir une tempête tropicale ayant un comportement similaire (cette tempête tropicale n°01, non baptisée, s'était toutefois formée un peu plus à l'est et avait impacté directement les îles de Praslin et La Digue).

LES TORTUES GEANTES DES SEYCHELLES, SAUVEES DE L'EXTINCTION.............MAIS TROP NOMBREUSE !!!

L' Atoll d'Aldabra, fait partie de l' archipel des Seychelles. C'est ici que vit la tortue, depuis la nuit des temps. Depuis que le continent Godwana ne faisait qu'un, il y a très très très longtemps. 
180 000 Tortues géantes d'Aldabra vivent aujourd'hui sur l' atoll. Elle sont plus nombreuses que les Humains, au nombre de 122 000 !!! Elles sont si nombreuses que les programmes de transfert de ces géantes, ont débuté sur d'autres atolls de l' Océan Indien ( Cousin, Mahé, Frégate ). 
Ces grosses mémères ( 1m20 et 250 kilos pour les mâles ) ne vivent qu'ici, exception faite d'un petit cheptel localisé aux îles Galapagos. L' atoll est l'un des derniers paradis de la planète Terre. Ecosystem intact et sauvetage remarquable....
Au XIXème siècle, la tortue a été massacrée. Il n'en restait que 1000 au milieu du XXème...En 1981, l'UNESCO prend les choses en main. La réussite est là, mais la vigilance est de mise, les sècheresses à répétition, déséquilibrent l'environnement et les tortues, trop nombreuses risquent de ne plus trouver de quoi manger suffisamment. La montée des eaux risquent également de perturber l' habitat de ces tortues terrestres.

stories.title: New Compensation Committee Criticised Over TRNUC Awards
stories.description: In a Facebook post published on 18 October 2026, the author criticises a new committee in Seychelles, headed by Mr Bibi, over its handling of compensation for victims addressed by the TRNUC. The author says the committee dismissed the previous offers and will decide compensation amounts, and questions its progress on 375 cases with determinations while expressing concern about delays and further distress to victims.

publications.text:
I have issues with what Mr Bibi stated in this interview, but for now I will wait to see what he proposes before I state what they all are. I will say, it seems by Mr Bibi’s attitude, that this new committee/commission supersedes the formal TRNUC commission with all it’s powers of the Supreme Court. President Faure instigated the commission, agreed to it’s remit and stated the victims should be paid in full what the TRNUC had offered, which is in guidelines with international regulations, while taking into account the financial status of Seychelles, but now as head of this new committee, Mr Bibi has dismissed the offers made by the previous TRNUC commission and stated that the new committee will decide the amount of repatriation/compensation given. stories.title: Military Airbase Plan for Aldabra (Seychelles) Did Not Proceed
stories.description: A video published on 22 October 2026 recounts that Aldabra (Seychelles) was considered for a military airbase in the 1960s. It says scientific research, opposition to the project and rising costs contributed to a different outcome; it does not specify when the proposal was dropped.

publications.title: Aldabra: el atolón que casi se convirtió en una base militar #atlasinalcanzable #historia #nature
publications.text:
Aldabra es un atolón remoto de Seychelles donde conviven tortugas gigantes, manglares y aves con una historia evolutiva extraordinaria. En los años sesenta, su ubicación en el océano Índico lo convirtió en candidato para una base aérea militar. La investigación científica, la oposición al proyecto y el aumento de los costes contribuyeron a un desenlace diferente.

En este episodio de Atlas Inalcanzable exploramos su laguna, la caliza formada por antiguos arrecifes y la relación entre las tortugas y la vegetación. También explicamos qué significa que los rascones perdieran el vuelo en dos ocasiones distintas, sin recurrir al mito de una especie que resucita.

El recorrido termina en los desafíos de conservar un lugar aislado: controlar las visitas, evitar nuevas introducciones y retirar residuos que llegan por el mar. La lejanía ayuda a limitar ciertas presiones, pero no desconecta al atolón del resto del planeta.

#AtlasInalcanzable #Aldabra #Seychelles

Fuentes:
- UNESCO — Aldabra Atoll.
- Seychelles Islands Foundation — historia, ecología y gestión de Aldabra.
- NASA Earth Observatory — An Outpost for Evolution at Aldabra Atoll.
- Royal Society — Atoll protected: proyecto militar y estación científica.
- Hume y Martill, 2019 — evolución repetida de la pérdida del vuelo; resumen del estudio.
- Estudio sobre la pérdida del vuelo y la divergencia de los rascones de Aldabra.
- Evaluación IUCN de conservación de Aldabra, 2020.
- SIF — reglamento de visitas publicado y plan de bioseguridad de 2021.
- UNESCO — retirada de 25 toneladas de residuos, noticia de 2020.

stories.title: FPAC Examines Procurement Quotation and Contract Gaps
stories.description: On 15 October 2026, the Finance and Public Accounts Committee (FPAC), chaired by the Leader of the Opposition (Bernard Georges), concluded its public hearings on the Auditor General’s Report for 2024 after a final hearing with the Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs. The committee examined the reported absence of alternative quotations and contracts in procurement processes and sought clarification on the circumstances and measures to strengthen controls, compliance and accountability.

publications.text:
On Thursday 15th October 2026, the Finance and Public Accounts Committee (FPAC) chaired by the Leader of the Opposition Hon. Bernard Georges, concluded its series of Public Hearings on the Auditor General’s Report for 2024 following its final hearing with the Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs.

Among the matters examined were issues relating to the absence of alternative quotations and the absence of alternative contracts in procurement processes. The Committee sought clarification on the circumstances surrounding these matters, as well as the measures in place to strengthen procurement controls, compliance, and accountability.

FPAC reiterated the importance of ensuring that procurement processes are conducted in accordance with established procedures and that adequate documentation and supporting records are maintained to demonstrate transparency, value for money, and accountability in the management of public resources.

The Committee remains committed to strengthening parliamentary oversight of public finances and ensuring that issues identified through the audit process are appropriately followed up and addressed.

The Department of Risk and Disaster Management (DRDM) wishes to provide an update on the prevailing weather conditions across Seychelles, following its earlier communiqué and in view of the continued guidance from the Seychelles Meteorological
Authority (SMA).

📍The situation regarding soil saturation remains high in several areas, and the risk of landslides, slope instability, falling trees and localised flooding persists should further rainfall occur.

📍Further information on reopening will
be communicated through official channels.

Members of the public are reminded to:
📍Remain informed through official weather forecasts and advisories issued by the relevant authorities.

📍Follow instructions and advisories issued through official government and
authorised information channels, and refrain from spreading rumours, hearsay
or unverified information that may cause unnecessary alarm or confusion.

📍Avoid unnecessary earthworks, excavation and activities near unstable slopes, particularly during periods of heavy rainfall.

📍Keep drainage channels clear, where it is safe to do so, to minimise the risk of
localised flooding.

📍Exercise caution when travelling, particularly along roads susceptible to
flooding, falling debris and landslides.

📍Remain attentive to any signs of ground movement, slope instability or other emerging hazards and report concerns promptly.

📍DRDM, through the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC), continues to monitor the situation in coordination with the SMA and relevant response agencies to maintain operational readiness and facilitate timely intervention where necessary.

📍The 160-emergency support line remains operational 24 hours a day, seven days a week, for reporting hazardous situations, emergencies or requests for emergency assistance.
