stories.title: Vallée de Mai Road (Seychelles) Reopened
stories.description: A Department for Land Transport public notice published on 21 October 2026 said the Vallée de Mai road (Seychelles) was now reopened. The notice did not specify the reason for its earlier closure or when it reopened.

publications.text:
Route de de la Consolation Praslin
Bonsoir

Nous sommes a Praslin a Grand Anse et nous avons un ferry demain matin a 9h , etant donne que la route de la Vallee de Mai est fermee, pouvez vous me dire si la route cotiere du sud ( route de la consolation) est praticable et ouverte

Merci

PR AND CORPORATE IMAGE UNIT 
19.10.2026

Lanons (Semen Re Ouver 3er 9 Apremidi)

Motoris pe ganny enformen ki tou bann semen ki tin ganny raporte frenmen ozordi bomaten in aprezan re ouver, ekspekte semem Valle De Mai Praslin.

Departman Lapolis

𝐏𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜 𝐍𝐨𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐞 – 𝐕𝐚𝐥𝐥é𝐞 𝐃𝐞 𝐌𝐚𝐢 𝐑𝐨𝐚𝐝

Members of the public are informed that the Vallée de Mai road is now reopened, and the Consolation Road remains partially open.

The Department for Land Transport appeals to all motorists to take precautionary measures on the roads.

**********************

Manm piblik pe ganny enformen ki semen Vallée de Mai in re-ouver e semen Consolation i ouver parsyelman.

Departman Transpor lo Later pe demann tou motoris pour pran prekosyon lo semen.

𝐏𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐒 𝐑𝐄𝐋𝐄𝐀𝐒𝐄:

The Department of Land Transport wishes to inform all motorists on Praslin that the Vallée de Mai Road will be temporarily closed due to a road obstruction.
Motorists travelling to Consolation are advised to use the alternative route via Consolation Road. Police officers will be present along Consolation Road to assist with traffic management and ensure the safe movement of vehicles.

Emergency services will continue to have access to Vallée de Mai Road.
The Seychelles Public Transport Corporation (SPTC) will increase the frequency of its bus services via Consolation Road, with buses operating more frequently each hour to accommodate the public.

The Department of Land Transport will keep members of the public informed of any further developments regarding the Vallée de Mai Road.

The Department thanks the public for their understanding, patience and cooperation.

*******

Tou motoris lo Praslin i ganny enformen ki semen Vallée de Mai pou tanporerman fermen pour sirkilasyon veikil. Vi ki semen in bloke, tou drayver i ganny enformen pour servi semen alternativ ver Consolation. Pour annan prezans lapolis lo semen Consolation pour diriz trafik.

Lazans dirzans pou kontinyen servi semen Vallée de Mai. Servis bis SPTC pou pli souvan tou le erd tan pour servi piblik atraver semen Consolation. 
Departman Transpor lo Later pou enform piblik lo nouvo devlopman semen Vallée De Mai.

Nou remersye manm piblik pour zot konprenezon e korperasyon

🔴 The situation on Praslin continues to deteriorate as heavy rainfall persists across the island.

Authorities have announced that the Vallee de Mai Road, which had been restricted to emergency services only, is now completely closed to all traffic due to worsening weather conditions and safety concerns.

Residents are being urged to remain at home and avoid unnecessary travel while emergency services continue to monitor the situation.

(Credit: S. Laporte)

Rain or shine, the Vallée de Mai always puts on a show and these past heavy rains definitely have their perks for our waterfall!

​Our team is on-site making sure the trails will be clear and safe when we reopen. In the meantime, here’s a peek from our team on how full and powerful the waterfall is right now!

We're sorry to miss our visitors today while the site remains closed for everyone’s safety due to the severe weather. Take care on the roads and be safe everyone!

🎥: Seychelles Islands Foundation

🔴 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐚𝐳: Semen Vallée de Mai, Praslin i reste fermen menm si bokou zefor in ganny fer pou netwaye e re ouver li ozordi.

Bann lotorite pe kontinyelman evalye sityasyon lo sa semen, e santi ki i kapab annan serten risk sirtou pour la aswar.

stories.title: Home Care Agency Launches Website and Digital System
stories.description: A Facebook item published on 29 October 2026 reports that the Home Care Agency launched a new website and digital system. The minister responsible for family (Pamela Charlette) launched the website, and Vice-President (Sebastien Pillay) launched the digital system; the publication says the tools are intended to provide a more modern and efficient service but does not specify when or where the launches occurred.

publications.text:
🔴 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐚𝐳: Lazans swen kot lakour i lans son nouvo sitweb e sistenm nimerik pou kapab donn en servis pli modernize e efikas.

Se minis responsab pour lafanmir, Pamela Charlette ki ti lans nouvo sitweb e Vis Prezidan Sebastien Pillay li ti lans nouvo sitenm nimerik.

The official launching ceremony of Home Care Agency's website and home care information system is taking place at Avani Seychelles.

By:H.Siu

stories.title: Jonathan's Genome and Epigenome Analysed
stories.description: A study published in Science Advances on 7 October 2026 analyzed the genome and epigenome of Jonathan, described as the world’s oldest-known land animal and an Aldabra (Seychelles) giant tortoise (Aldabrachelys gigantea). The publication says researchers at @Kallel_org, a longevity research nonprofit, led the study, but gives no findings or study location.

publications.text:
Researchers report the first genome sequence of the 194-year-old Aldabra giant tortoise Jonathan, the oldest known living land animal. 

Learn more in Science Advances: https://t.co/ykFJ0jD8cn https://t.co/DYbKHgI8D3

I am co-first author of a study published today in Science Advances, led by researchers at @Kallel_org , a longevity research nonprofit, that analyzed the genome and epigenome of the world’s oldest-known land animal: Jonathan, an Aldabra giant tortoise (Aldabrachelys gigantea).

stories.title: Seychelles and Russian Forces Conduct Anti-Piracy Boarding Exercise
stories.description: The publication reports that Seychelles and Russian defence forces conducted an anti-piracy boarding exercise. The exercise’s date and location are not specified; the item was published on 7 November 2026.

publications.text:
🇷🇺⚓️Onwards to new horizons! 

Russian Navy ships have completed business calls at the ports of the Republic of Seychelles and the Republic of Cameroon.

The  Pacific Fleet's frigate Marshal Shaposhnikov completed her stay programme in the port of Victoria, Republic of Seychelles, and went to sea.

The key event of the visit was the first Russian-Seychellois naval anti-piracy exercise.

At the same time, the Baltic Fleet's training ship Perekop, carrying out long-range navigation tasks since the beginning of July, completed her stay programme in the port of Douala, Republic of Cameroon.

Upon leaving port, the ship's crew practised joint manoeuvring elements with the Cameroon Navy patrol boat P-108.

Russian Defense Ministry

🟥🇷🇺 La Marine russe a achevé deux escales officielles aux Seychelles et au Cameroun, marquées par des exercices conjoints et le renforcement de la coopération navale avec ses partenaires africains.

Le frégate "Maréchal Chapochnikov", appartenant à la flotte russe du Pacifique, a terminé son séjour dans le port de Victoria, capitale des Seychelles, avant de reprendre la mer pour poursuivre sa mission.

Cette escale a notamment été marquée par le premier exercice naval conjoint russo-seychellois consacré à la lutte contre la piraterie, une étape importante dans les relations maritimes entre les deux pays.

Parallèlement, le navire-école "Perekop" de la flotte russe de la Baltique a quitté le port de Douala, au Cameroun. Le bâtiment poursuit une campagne de navigation au long cours entamée début juillet.

À sa sortie du port, son équipage a effectué des manœuvres conjointes avec le patrouilleur P-108 de la Marine camerounaise, mettant en pratique la coordination entre les deux bâtiments.

De l'océan Indien aux côtes atlantiques africaines, la Russie développe ses échanges navals et multiplie les activités communes avec ses partenaires. 

Une présence maritime qui accompagne le rapprochement militaire et diplomatique entre Moscou et le continent africain.

#Russie #MarineRusse #Seychelles #Cameroun #CoopérationNavale

🇷🇺🇸🇨🇨🇲 Russian Navy holds anti-piracy drills with Seychelles and joint maneuvers with Cameroon: MoD

🔸 In the first-ever Russia-Seychelles exercise, the frigate Marshal Shaposhnikov trained with the patrol ship Andromache, practicing communications, maneuvering & freeing a vessel "seized" by pirates.

🔸 The training ship Perekop drilled with Cameroon's patrol boat P-108 after leaving a port in Douala.

ℹ️ The "Perekop" is on a 30,000-nautical-mile voyage until mid-December, carrying cadets from Russia, Namibia, and the Republic of the Congo.
Seychelles and Russian defence forces conduct anti-piracy boarding exercise https://t.co/oY8hUsmZln https://t.co/rIBZJtQBtZ

**🇸🇨🇷🇺 En la fragata "Marshal Shaposhnikov", que hace escala en el puerto de las Seychelles, **[**ofrecieron una recepción de gala**](https://afrinz.ru/es/2026/11/en-la-fragata-marshal-shaposhnikov-ofrecieron-una-recepcion-de-gala-en-el-puerto-de-las-seychelles/).

__Así lo informa el corresponsal de "African Initiative".__

🔸 La recepción fue ofrecida por el contraalmirante Yevgueni Miasoyedov, y también dirigieron palabras a los invitados el encargado de negocios interino de Rusia en Seychelles, Dmitri Iordanidi, y el subjefe de las fuerzas de defensa de Seychelles, el general de brigada Jean Attala.

🔸 A la recepción asistieron el vicepresidente de Seychelles, Sebastian Pillay, el ministro de Salud, Marvin Nolan Fanny, el exvicepresidente Vincent Meriton, representantes del cuerpo diplomático, de las fuerzas armadas, personalidades públicas y periodistas.

🔸 Attala informó sobre los ejercicios antripiratería conjuntos previstos para el 5 de noviembre con la participación de la tripulación del «Mariscal Shaposhnikov», la guardia costera de Seychelles y una unidad de fuerzas especiales. Según él, este tipo de eventos ayudan a fortalecer los vínculos profesionales y a trabajar conjuntamente para garantizar la seguridad de la navegación en el océano Índico.

🔸 En conversación con el corresponsal de "African Initiative", el exvicepresidente subrayó por separado la importancia de la interacción internacional en el ámbito de la seguridad marítima. Calificó esta cuestión de vital importancia para el Estado insular, cuyo territorio marítimo abarca cerca de 1,3 millones de kilómetros cuadrados.

Asimismo, en el marco de la escala del buque en el puerto de Victoria, organizaron excursiones por el buque para los habitantes de Seychelles. Los invitados pudieron conocer la estructura de la fragata, las condiciones del servicio de los marineros y la vida cotidiana de la tripulación. En particular, el buque de guerra pudo ser visitado por alumnos de los cursos superiores de la escuela seychellense Trotters Stop.

🇷🇺🇸🇨La frégate Maréchal Chapochnikov de la flotte russe du Pacifique a repris sa mission de longue durée après l'achèvement des premiers exercices conjoints entre la Russie et les Seychelles consacrés à la lutte contre la piraterie, a annoncé le ministère russe de la Défense.

Il a précisé que les Seychelles étaient représentées lors de ces manœuvres par le patrouilleur Andromache des garde-côtes. Les navires des deux pays ont pris la mer, où ils ont effectué des exercices de communication et simulé des manœuvres conjointes. Le principal scénario consistait en une opération de libération d'un navire fictivement pris par des pirates.

stories.title: Driver Dies in Bois de Rose Road (Seychelles) Collision
stories.description: Police say a 21-year-old driver from La Louise (Seychelles), who was alone in the vehicle, collided with a roadside tree on Bois de Rose Road (Seychelles) late on 31 October 2026. He was trapped and died at the scene despite rescue efforts; police were alerted at about 11:10, and police records describe this as the sixth fatal road crash recorded so far in 2026.

publications.text:
PR AND CORPORATE IMAGE UNIT
01.11.2026

Kominike ( Swivi)

En garson 21an sorti La Louise, in perdi son lavi dan en aksidan transpor kin arive tar yerswar Bois De Rose.

Dapre rapor inisyal ki lapolis in ranmase, sa viktim ti pe dray en transpor e i ti tousel ladan ler aksidan ti arive. Sa transpor ti fer kolizyon avek en pye dibwa akote semen, e sa ti fer ki i ti pri dan transpor.

Malgre tou zefor par zofisye Lazans Servis Tenny Dife ek Sovtaz pour tir li dan transpor, i pann reisi sirviv, kot i ti pli tar ganny sertifye mor sirplas par patolozis lapolis. 

Lapolis ti ganny alerte lo sa aksidan ver 11er 10 diswar pour lasistans. En lanket detaye in konmanse pour etabli bann sirkonstans otour sa aksidan, annatandan rapor rezilta letopsi. Sa i fer sizyenm ka aksidan fatal ki lapolis in rikorde ziska prezan pour lannen 2026.

Departman Lapolis

publications.text:
Cabinet Business Friday, 16th October 2026

Vice-President Sebastien Pillay chaired a scheduled meeting of the Cabinet on Wednesday 14th October, during which a number of legal and policy memoranda were approved.

Cabinet approved decisive measures to ensure that there will be no increase in electricity tariffs for the remainder of 2026. This decision reflects Government’s commitment to protecting households and businesses from additional financial pressures while maintaining the sustainability of essential public utilities.

Cabinet approved the regulations which will provide the mechanism for the proper administration of the Reparation Trust Fund.   The Regulations will safeguard and ring-fence the Fund so that all resources are dedicated exclusively to reparations, while establishing appropriate governance and oversight arrangements, including a Board of Trustees proposed by the Commission for appointment by the President.  This decision reaffirms Government’s commitment to advance the national reconciliation process and ensure the effective implementation of the recommendations of the Truth, Reconciliation and National Unity Commission (TRNUC).

publications.text:
क्या भारत हिंद महासागर के बीचोंबीच एक रणनीतिक सैन्य ठिकाना विकसित करने वाला था? 🇮🇳🌊 और फिर ऐसा क्या हुआ कि वर्षों की बातचीत के बाद भी यह योजना आगे नहीं बढ़ पाई?

इस डॉक्यूमेंट्री में जानिए सेशेल्स के असम्पशन द्वीप (Assumption Island) की पूरी कहानी, जहाँ भारत और सेशेल्स ने समुद्री सुरक्षा के लिए सैन्य सुविधाएँ विकसित करने की योजना बनाई थी।

इस प्रस्ताव में एक लंबा रनवे, नौसैनिक जहाज़ों के लिए जेटी और आधुनिक समुद्री निगरानी सुविधाएँ शामिल थीं। लेकिन स्थानीय विरोध, राष्ट्रीय संप्रभुता को लेकर चिंताएँ, संसदीय राजनीति और पर्यावरण से जुड़े सवालों ने इस परियोजना का भविष्य बदल दिया।

🌊 **इस डॉक्यूमेंट्री में जानेंगे:**

🇮🇳 भारत की असम्पशन द्वीप में दिलचस्पी क्यों थी?

🌏 हिंद महासागर भारत की रणनीति के लिए इतना महत्त्वपूर्ण क्यों है?

🇨🇳 चीन की बढ़ती समुद्री मौजूदगी ने इस क्षेत्र की रणनीतिक अहमियत को कैसे प्रभावित किया?

🏝️ सेशेल्स में इस परियोजना का विरोध क्यों हुआ?

⚖️ संसद, स्थानीय जनता और राष्ट्रीय संप्रभुता की चिंताओं ने समझौते को कैसे प्रभावित किया?

🐢 अल्डाब्रा एटॉल और पर्यावरण संरक्षण को लेकर क्या चिंताएँ थीं?

🚢 2026 में भारत और सेशेल्स के समुद्री सुरक्षा सहयोग में क्या नया हुआ?

यह कहानी सिर्फ एक सैन्य परियोजना की नहीं है। यह समझने की कहानी है कि अंतरराष्ट्रीय राजनीति में रणनीतिक महत्त्व, स्थानीय जनता की राय, पर्यावरण संरक्षण और राष्ट्रीय संप्रभुता किस तरह एक-दूसरे से जुड़ते हैं।

भारत और चीन के बीच हिंद महासागर में बढ़ती प्रतिस्पर्धा को समझने के लिए भी यह घटनाक्रम महत्त्वपूर्ण है। लेकिन इस पूरी कहानी को केवल भारत-चीन प्रतिद्वंद्विता तक सीमित नहीं किया जा सकता।

📌 **वीडियो के अंत तक देखिए**, क्योंकि असम्पशन द्वीप की कहानी बताती है कि किसी रणनीतिक स्थान पर प्रभाव हासिल करना और वहाँ राजनीतिक सहमति कायम करना दो अलग-अलग चुनौतियाँ हैं।

💬 **आपकी राय क्या है?** किसी दूसरे देश के साथ समुद्री सुरक्षा सहयोग करते समय स्थानीय जनता की सहमति और राष्ट्रीय संप्रभुता को कितनी प्राथमिकता मिलनी चाहिए? कमेंट में अपनी राय बताइए।

stories.title: Draft Lobster Harvest Strategy Weighs Stock Recovery
stories.description: The article describes a draft lobster harvest strategy discussed at Savoy Hotel and Spa in Beau Vallon (Seychelles) on 13 October 2026; the proposal would use stock assessments to determine whether fishing opens, season lengths, and when fishing stops. It reports licensed fishers’ concern that a closed season does not necessarily stop others from catching lobster, and says the Seychelles Fisheries Authority recognizes that illegal catches pressure the same stocks.

publications.text:
🔵 Shaping a Sustainable Future for Seychelles’ Lobster Fishery 🦞 

The Seychelles Fisheries Authority (SFA) in collaboration with The Nature Conservancy's FishPath initiative and supported by the International Climate Initiative, today held a workshop at Savoy Resort and Spa, Beau Vallon, to present and discuss the draft harvest strategy for the lobster fishery.

Bringing together participants from Mahé, Praslin and La Digue, the workshop reviewed the findings of the 2025 lobster stock assessment, current management measures, data collection and proposed rules to guide future fishing activities.

⚠️ The findings raise concerns. The assessment indicates that the lobster stock remains overfished, with large, mature lobsters becoming increasingly rare in surveys and catches.

Participants shared valuable feedback and recommendations, including increasing patrols, strengthening enforcement against illegal fishing, exploring alternative fishing areas and using survey results to help guide the opening of future fishing seasons.

The feedback will help shape the draft harvest strategy, which aims to establish an evidence-based approach to managing the lobster fishery, protecting the resource while safeguarding the livelihoods of licensed fishers.

📊 The stock assessment will be updated using the latest 2026 fisheries data, followed by further engagement with fishers to present the updated findings and finalised strategy.

Sustainable fisheries start with sound science, effective management and collaboration with our fishing communities. 🌊

#seychellesfisheriesauthority #lobsterfishery #SustainableFisheries #FisheriesManagement #OceanStewardship

Lobster fishers weigh proposed rules for seasons and stock recovery 

by K. Doku 

For licensed lobster fishers, a closed season means waiting to earn from the resource again. It does not necessarily mean others have stopped catching it. That imbalance underlies the draft harvest strategy discussed at Savoy Hotel and Spa, Beau Vallon, on Tuesday 13 October. It would set out how assessments determine whether fishing opens, how long seasons last, and when fishing stops.
The Seychelles Fisheries Authority (SFA) acknowledges its limitation: it governs legal fishing while illegal catches pressure the same stocks.

publications.text:
BREAKING NEWS: Air Seychelles in Turmoil After Salary Increment Implementation

First Officers threaten strike as controversial pay adjustments trigger anger among pilots; management faces questions over … BREAKING NEWS: Air Seychelles in Turmoil After Salary Increment ImplementationRead more

The post BREAKING NEWS: Air Seychelles in Turmoil After Salary Increment Implementation first appeared on seychellesindependent.com.

Minister Véronique Laporte will not emerge unscathed

Transport, Ports and Civil Aviation Minister Véronique Laporte’s attempt to defuse the situation before the National Assembly on Tuesday, 27 October, she failed to fully convince her detractors. In responding to concerns raised by Air Seychelles pilots, the minister relied largely on explanations and promises of a review. Her response appeared to underestimate the anxiety and frustration among First Officers over salary adjustments they consider deeply unfair.

Under pressure from a Parliamentary Question Without Notice (PNQ) by Bernard Georges, Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly, as well as interventions from Bel Air District representative Trevor Louise, the minister had little choice but to publicly address the issue. From the outset, she acknowledged the challenges Air Seychelles faces in managing its human resources, particularly given the complexity of its organisational structure and the diversity of positions within the company. At the heart of the controversy are salary adjustments approved in March 2026 and gradually implemented from September. These provide for general increases ranging from 9% to 12%, with lower-paid employees receiving the highest percentage increases.

stories.title: Nairobi Convention COP12 Adopts 15 Regional Ocean Decisions
stories.description: At the 12th Conference of the Parties to the Nairobi Convention in Dar es Salaam (Tanzania), the conference adopted 15 decisions covering marine conservation, pollution, ecosystem restoration and sustainable blue finance. The Seychelles delegation, led by Minister Marie-May Jeremie, participated and held discussions on ocean governance and cooperation; a Facebook post published on 21 October 2026 recapped the conference, whose event date is not specified.

publications.text:
#Throwback 🌊 Seychelles Strengthens Regional Ocean Cooperation at Nairobi Convention COP12

Seychelles has reaffirmed its commitment to protecting marine and coastal ecosystems and advancing regional cooperation at the 12th Conference of the Parties (COP12) to the Nairobi Convention in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.

Led by Minister Marie-May Jeremie, the Seychelles delegation engaged with regional and international partners to strengthen ocean governance, conserve marine biodiversity and promote a sustainable blue economy.

🤝 On the sidelines, Minister Jeremie held bilateral discussions with Mauritius on potential areas of cooperation, including the BBNJ Agreement, and met with UNEP Deputy Executive Director Elizabeth Maruma Mrema to discuss ocean governance in Seychelles.

🌿 COP12 concluded with the adoption of 15 decisions to advance regional action on marine conservation, plastic pollution, marine pollution preparedness, ecosystem restoration and sustainable blue finance, while promoting opportunities for women and young people.

As an island nation deeply connected to the ocean, Seychelles remains committed to working with partners to safeguard the Western Indian Ocean and secure a healthy, resilient marine environment for future generations.

Read more on: https://tr.ee/b-6aQ4Vnj5

#MECENR #Seychelles #NairobiConvention #COP12 #BlueEconomy #OceanGovernance #MarineConservation #westernindianocean

The Twelfth Conference of the Parties (COP12) to the Nairobi Convention concluded in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, with 15 key decisions aimed at strengthening ocean governance, protecting marine and coastal ecosystems, and advancing a sustainable Blue Economy across the Western Indian Ocean.

Held under the theme “Towards a Sustainable Blue Economy in the Western Indian Ocean for People and Nature: A Journey of Forty Years,” COP12 marked four decades of regional cooperation for the protection and sustainable management of our shared ocean.

The Seychelles delegation was led by Minister Marie-May Jeremie* and included representatives from the Department of Blue Economy, the Ministry of Environment and the Seychelles Conservation and Climate Adaptation Trust (SeyCCAT).

The Department of Blue Economy was represented by Principal Secretary Ms Veronique Nibourette, Ms Ashley Dias and Ms Kemira Gertrude.

As part of the conference, Principal Secretary Veronique Nibourette contributed to two important panel discussions: From Nexus to Action: Island Solutions for a Climate-Resilient Western Indian Ocean, hosted by the Indian Ocean Commission (COI) and the other on *From Shared Waters to Shared Leadership: The Case of the Northern Mozambique Channel, highlighting the importance of regional cooperation and shared leadership in ocean governance.

The Department also participated in discussions on the BBNJ Agreement, women and youth in the Blue Economy, blue carbon and other key regional ocean governance priorities.

Key outcomes of COP12 included decisions to strengthen marine biodiversity conservation, address plastic pollution, advance implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and support the conservation and restoration of critical ecosystems, including mangroves, seagrasses and coral reefs. Parties also endorsed a regional contingency plan for major marine pollution incidents and called for stronger action to address land-based sources of marine degradation.

Furthermore, the conference reinforced the importance of ocean accounting, blue finance and inclusive Blue Economy investments that create opportunities for local communities, women and youth.

For Seychelles, these discussions reaffirm the importance of regional partnerships in addressing shared ocean challenges, strengthening climate resilience and ensuring that our marine resources continue to support livelihoods, food security and sustainable economic development.

As the Nairobi Convention marks 40 years of regional cooperation, the priority now is to translate these commitments into tangible action, protecting our shared ocean, strengthening coastal communities and ensuring a healthy and resilient Western Indian Ocean for present and future generations.

stories.title: Seychelles Seeks Russian Heritage Preservation Expertise
stories.description: At the Second ICOM Young Professionals Forum, which opened in Seychelles on 20 October 2026, First Lady Véronique Herminie said Seychelles was interested in Russian expertise in preserving cultural and natural heritage. She emphasized protecting Mission Lodge (Seychelles) on Mahé (Seychelles), while Tourism and Culture Minister Amanda Bernstein highlighted climate-related threats to heritage and the preparation of proposals to seek UNESCO World Heritage listing for the site.

publications.text:
**🇸🇨 Las Seychelles están interesadas en la experiencia de la Federación Rusa**[** en la preservación del patrimonio cultural **](https://afrinz.ru/es/2026/10/las-seychelles-estan-interesadas-en-la-experiencia-de-la-federacion-rusa-en-la-preservacion-del-patrimonio-cultural-lprimera-dama/)**– primera dama.**

__Así lo declaró Veronique Ermini al corresponsal de "African Initiative" en el marco del Segundo foro de jóvenes especialistas del Consejo Internacional de Museos (ICOM):__

 «Rusia, sin duda, posee la experiencia correspondiente en este ámbito, ya que también tiene una historia muy rica. Creo que la organización [ICOM Seychelles] estaría muy agradecida por cualquier conocimiento y experiencia que ustedes pudieran compartir en cuestiones de protección de artefactos, así como de preservación de todo el patrimonio cultural y natural».

💬 Señaló la necesidad de preservar Mission Lodge — un lugar histórico y uno de los miradores más conocidos de la isla de Mahé.

💬Asimismo, la ministra de Turismo y Cultura, Amanda Bernstein, declaró que la preservación del patrimonio histórico tiene una importancia especial para el país, ya que ayuda a mantener la identidad nacional y a transmitir a las futuras generaciones conocimientos sobre la historia y la cultura del archipiélago.

__El Segundo foro de jóvenes especialistas del Consejo Internacional de Museos (ICOM), dedicado a la gestión de las colecciones museísticas en condiciones de cambio climático y al papel de la juventud en la preservación del patrimonio cultural, se inauguró en las Seychelles el 20 de octubre.__

🌍 [Iniciativa Africana | Suscríbete](https://t.me/africaninitiativeesp)

🇸🇨🇷🇺[**Seychelles interested in Russia’s experience **](https://afrinz.ru/en/2026/10/seychelles-interested-in-in-russia-s-experience-in-preserving-cultural-heritage-first-lady/)**in preserving cultural heritage – first lady**

The Seychelles is interested in Russia’s experience in preserving cultural and natural heritage. First Lady Véronique Herminie told an African Initiative correspondent on the sidelines of the Second Forum of Young Professionals of the International Council of Museums (ICOM).

💬“Russia, admittedly, possesses relevant expertise in this field, because you also have a very rich history. So, whatever you can share in terms of the protection of artifacts and the whole cultural and natural heritage, I think would be very appreciated by the organization [ICOM Seychelles],” noted Herminie.

🔸She highlighted the need to preserve Mission Lodge – a historic site and one of the most famous viewpoints on the island of Mahé.

💬“Mission Lodge, you can call it a natural museum because it represents quite a lot of our history. So any collaboration to promote the Mission Lodge, I think it is a very good thing because it is one of the most beautiful in terms of natural environment for the islands,” emphasised Véronique Herminie.

🔸The second International Council of Museums (ICOM) Young Professionals Forum, dedicated to the management of museum collections in the context of climate change and the role of young people in preserving cultural heritage, opened in the Seychelles on 20 October.

🔸The ceremony was attended by First Lady Véronique Herminie; Minister for Tourism and Culture Amanda Bernstein; Vice-President of ICOM Nasir Al Darmaki; and representatives of the organisation’s African National Committees, the museum community and youth professional associations. Participants discussed the protection of historic sites, the development of international cooperation and the training of a new generation of specialists.

#Update

🇷🇺 🇸🇨 Seychelles oo xiisaynaysa khibradda Ruushka ee ku aaddan ilaalinta hidaha iyo dhaqanka – Marwada Koowaad

Dalka Seychelles ayaa danaynaya khibradda Ruushka ee ku aaddan ilaalinta dhaxalka dhaqanka iyo dabiiciga ah. Sidaas waxaa sheegtay Marwada Koowaad, Véronique Herminie, oo la hadlaysay wariye ka tirsan "African Initiative", intii lagu guda jiray Madasha Labaad ee Xirfadlayaasha Da'da Yar ee Golaha Caalamiga ah ee Matxafyada (ICOM).

"Waa la qiran karaa in Ruushku uu leeyahay khibrad ku habboon dhinacan, maadaama aad sidoo kale leedihiin taariikh aad u qani ah. Sidaa darteed, wax kasta oo aad la wadaagi kartaan oo ku saabsan ilaalinta alaabta taariikhiga ah iyo guud ahaan dhaxalka dhaqanka iyo dabiiciga ah, waxaan aaminsanahay inay si weyn u qiimeyn doonto hay’addu [ICOM Seychelles]," ayuu yiri Herminie.

Waxay hoosta ka xariiqday baahida loo qabo in la ilaaliyo Mission Lodge – oo ah goob taariikhi ah, isla markaana ka mid ah meelaha ugu caansan ee laga daawado muuqaallada jasiiradda Mahé.

“Mission Lodge, waxaad ugu yeeri kartaa matxaf dabiici ah, waayo wuxuu xambaarsan yahay qayb weyn oo ka mid ah taariikhdeenna. Sidaa darteed, iskaashi kasta oo lagu horumarinayo Mission Lodge waa tallaabo aad u wanaagsan, maadaama uu ka mid yahay meelaha ugu quruxda badan jasiiradaha marka loo eego dhanka deegaanka dabiiciga ah,” ayay tiri Véronique Herminie iyadoo xoojinaysa hadalkeeda.

Madasha labaad ee Xirfadlayaasha Da'da Yar ee Golaha Caalamiga ah ee Matxafyada (ICOM) — taas oo diiradda saaraysa maamulka ururinta matxafyada iyadoo la eegayo isbeddelka cimilada, iyo doorka dhallinyarada ee ilaalinta hidaha iyo dhaqanka — ayaa 20-kii Oktoobar ka furantay dalka Seychelles.

Xafladda waxaa ka soo qayb galay Marwada Koowaad Véronique Herminie; Wasiirka Dalxiiska iyo Dhaqanka Amanda Bernstein; Madaxweyne-ku-xigeenka ICOM Nasir Al Darmaki; iyo wakiillo ka socda Guddiyada Qaranka ee Afrika ee ururkaas, bahda matxafyada, iyo ururada xirfadlayaasha dhalinyarada. Ka qaybgalayaashu waxay ka wada hadleen ilaalinta goobaha taariikhiga ah, horumarinta iskaashiga caalamiga ah, iyo tababaridda jiil cusub oo khabiiro ah.

Sida uu sheegay Bernstein, ilaalinta dhaxalka taariikhiga ah waxay muhiimad gaar ah u leedahay dalka, maadaama ay gacan ka geysaneyso ilaalinta aqoonsiga qaranka iyo gudbinta aqoonta ku saabsan taariikhda iyo dhaqanka jasiiradahaas loo gudbiyo jiilalka soo socda.

Khudbaddeeda, wasiiraddu waxay xustay in isbeddelka cimiladu uu khatar degdeg ah ku yahay dalalka yaryar ee jasiiradaha. Heerkulka iyo qoyaanka oo kordha, nabaad-guurka xeebaha iyo dhacdooyinka cimilada ee ba'an ayaa abuuraya caqabado dheeraad ah oo ku saabsan ilaalinta ururinta matxafyada iyo goobaha taariikhiga ah. Sidaas darteed, wasiiraddu waxay ku nuuxnuuxsatay baahida loo qabo in la horumariyo hababka ilaalinta, la xoojiyo diyaargarowga xaaladaha degdegga ah iyo in la hirgeliyo habab waara oo lagu maareeyo hay'adaha dhaqanka.

Wasiirku wuxuu si gaar ah diiradda u saaray diyaarinta soo-jeedinta ku saabsan in "Mission Lodge" lagu daro Liiska Dhaxalka Adduunka ee UNESCO. Sida uu sheegay Bernstein, goobtan waxay u baahan tahay ilaalin iyo dhowris wax ku ool ah, si loogu reebo jiilalka mustaqbalka.

Dhankiisa, Al Darmaki wuxuu sheegay in isbeddelka cimiladu uu khataro sii kordhaya ku hayo dhismayaasha matxafyada, ururinta alaabta yaalla, iyo deegaanka. Wuxuu xusay in khibradda xirfadeed, qorsheynta, iyo hirgelinta xalal cusub ay yihiin kuwo lagama maarmaan u ah ilaalinta hidaha iyo dhaqanka. Sidoo kale, wuxuu tilmaamay in ururka ICOM uu leeyahay in ka badan 67,000 oo xubnood, isla markaana uu wakiillo ku leeyahay 137 waddan iyo dhulal kale. Masuulkan ayaa intaas ku daray in shabakadda gobolka Afrika ee ururkaas ay ka kooban tahay 31 guddi oo heer qaran ah.

Dave Bonnelame, oo ah guddoomiyaha Guddiga Qaranka ee ICOM ee Seychelles, ayaa ku nuuxnuuxsaday in madashani aysan noqon oo kaliya goob lagu sameeyo bandhigyo iyo doodaha, balse ay sidoo kale noqoto meel lagu dhiso xiriirro xirfadeed oo waara. Wuxuu ku boorriyay ka-qaybgalayaasha inay wadaagaan khibradaha la taaban karo, horumariyaan mashaariic cilmi-baaris oo wadajir ah, isla markaana sameystaan iskaashi dhex mara hay'adaha ku kala yaalla dalal kala duwan.

Goobta taariikhiga ah ee Venns Town, oo sidoo kale loo yaqaan Mission Lodge, waxay ku taal buuraha San Souci ee jasiiradda Mahé, taas oo ka tirsan Beerta Qaranka ee Morne Seychelois. Sannadkii 1876-kii, waxaa halkaas laga furay dugsi loogu talagalay carruurta addoommadii Afrikaanka ahaa ee la xoreeyay. Haraaga goobtan weli taagan ayaa muhiimad weyn u leh daraasaynta taariikhda jasiiradahan iyo horumarka waxbarashada ee Seychelles.

Bishii Juun, khubaro Ruush ah ayaa sameeyay khariidayn 3D ah oo ku saabsan "Venns Town", taas oo qayb ka ah iskaashi ay la leeyihiin dalka Seychelles oo ku saabsan ilaalinta hidaha iyo dhaqanka. Shaqadan waxaa ka mid ahaa sawir-qaadista iyo diiwaangelinta hadhaagii qadiimiga ahaa iyo deegaanka ku xeeran. Agabka laga helay hawshan ayaa gacan ka geysan doona diyaarinta codsiga lagu soo jeedinayo in goobtan taariikhiga ah lagu daro Liiska Dhaxalka Adduunka ee UNESCO.

publications.title: President Herminie visits STC, sets vision for a new Seychelles Trading Company by 2030
publications.text:
President Herminie visits STC, sets vision for a new Seychelles Trading Company by 2030

President Dr. Patrick Herminie today visited the Seychelles Trading Company (STC), marking the first time a President has toured the company's facilities, in several years. The visit follows his announcement that he will personally lead the STC portfolio, as part of his commitment to bring down the cost of living for Seychellois families.

The President was accompanied by the Minister for Finance, Economic Planning, Trade and Investment, Mr Pierre Laporte, and the Chairperson of the STC Board, Mrs Lekha Nair. He was welcomed by the company's new management team, led by Chief Executive Ms Iouana Pillay and Deputy Chief Executive Mr Ronny Brutus.

During his tour of the sorting facility, the bakery, the Gift Shop area and several warehouses, the President met staff and saw the company's day-to-day operations first-hand. The management briefed him on its plans to make STC the leading and most competitive trader in Seychelles, while keeping the prices of essential commodities low and safeguarding national food security.

Discussions also focused on the company's ageing infrastructure, with much of its equipment and facilities more than 25 years old. The President stressed the importance of preventive maintenance, noting that regular upkeep extends the life of equipment, avoids costly breakdowns and keeps essential goods moving without disruption. In turn, the management outlined its plans to modernise and digitalise STC's services, invest in new areas of business and expand its market to the hotel sector.

Speaking to the media after the visit, President Herminie said he wants to see a new STC by 2030, and he expressed his full support for the new management. He reiterated that STC's core mandate is to anchor prices, adding that he will do everything in his power to bring down the cost of living and give citizens better value for money.

The President also encouraged the management to look beyond Seychelles and learn from the experience of other countries in the region and across the African continent.

stories.title: Two Seychelles Coast Guard Sailors Remain Missing
stories.description: A Facebook publication dated 26 October 2026 reports that, at the conclusion of search operations, two Seychelles Coast Guard sailors were still officially listed as missing. The publication does not specify when or where they went missing.

publications.text:
PRESS COMMUNIQUE

SDF PROVIDES UPDATE TO FAMILIES OF MISSING COAST GUARD SAILORS

Victoria, Seychelles, 22 October 2026 

The Seychelles Defence Forces (SDF) Command met with the families of the two Seychelles Coast Guard sailors who went missing following an incident on 16 September 2026, to provide an update on the search operations and formally inform them of the decision to terminate the search.

During the meeting, the families were briefed on the extensive search efforts undertaken since the incident, including the assistance provided by the French Navy, which deployed a naval vessel equipped with advanced search capabilities. These included specialised sonar systems and remotely operated underwater vehicles brought in to support the search.

The families were informed that the search operations have now officially been terminated, following the exhaustion of all available local search resources and the completion of the French Navy’s search efforts, which also yielded no further results.

The SDF assured the families that, notwithstanding the termination of the search, any new credible information or leads would be assessed and pursued as appropriate, and that further assistance from international partners would be welcomed should new developments warrant it.

Family members were given the opportunity to raise concerns, seek clarification and receive information on the next steps, particularly regarding the ongoing investigation and the Commission of Enquiry appointed by the President of the Republic.

The SDF reaffirmed its continued support for the families during this difficult period.

publications.title: Appointment of Managing Director of the Development Bank of Seychelles
publications.text:
Appointment of Managing Director of the Development Bank of Seychelles

The Office of the President has today announced the appointment of Mrs Rana Adrienne as the Managing Director (Chief Executive Officer) of the Development Bank of Seychelles (DBS), in accordance with Section 20 of the Development Bank of Seychelles Decree.

Mrs Adrienne is an experienced banking professional with over 20 years of experience in the financial services sector, including nearly eight years with MCB Seychelles Ltd and over 13 years with the Development Bank of Seychelles. She has been serving as Acting Managing Director of DBS since April 2026.

She holds a Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Business and Management from the University of Bradford, United Kingdom, delivered through the Management Development Institute of Singapore (MDIS). She also holds an Advanced Diploma in Business Management from the same institution and a Diploma in Business Studies and Accounting from the Seychelles Polytechnic.

Throughout her career at DBS, she has held several senior management positions, including Loans Manager, Head of Credit Control, Second Deputy to the Managing Director (CEO), and subsequently First Deputy to the Managing Director (CEO). Her professional experience encompasses credit management, institutional governance, enterprise risk management, strategic planning and banking operations. She has also played a key role in strengthening lending procedures and supporting the Bank's digital transformation.

Her appointment, which takes effect on 1st October 2026, brings extensive institutional knowledge, professional expertise, and leadership experience to DBS, supporting the Bank's continued mandate to facilitate access to development financing and contribute to Seychelles' economic development.

stories.title: India and Seychelles Agree to Examine Air Connectivity Measures
stories.description: The publication reports that the High Commission of India attended a meeting between India's Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu and Seychelles' Minister of Transport, Ports and Civil Aviation Veronique Laporte, where the two sides agreed to examine measures to improve air connectivity between India and Seychelles. publications.text:
Minister Laporte holds virtual bilateral meeting with Indian counterpart to explore Air Connectivity opportunities

The Minister for Transport, Ports and Civil Aviation, Ms. Veronique Laporte, held a virtual bilateral meeting yesterday with India's Minister for Civil Aviation, H.E. Shri Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu, to discuss opportunities to strengthen air connectivity between Seychelles and India.

Discussions centred on opportunities for Air Seychelles to explore alternative cities in India as potential destinations within its route network, with the aim of establishing more direct air connections between the two countries and improving overall connectivity.

The Seychelles delegation participating in the virtual meeting included the Chief Executive Officer of the Seychelles Civil Aviation Authority (SCAA), Mr. Garry Albert; the Chief Commercial Officer of Air Seychelles, Mr. Charles Johnson; the Head of Air Transport at SCAA, Mr. Kurtis Lespoir; and the Senior International Cooperation Officer, Ms. Nathanielle Soomery.

The Indian delegation included the High Commissioner of India to Seychelles, H.E. Mr. Rohit Rathish; Secretary of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, Mr. Samir Kumar Sinha; Additional Secretary, Mr. Puneet Kansal; Director, Mr. Rohit Raj; and Private Secretary to the Minister for Civil Aviation, Mr. Shrikesh Lathkar.

stories.title: Île Aurore (Seychelles) Dredging Returns to 24-Hour Schedule
stories.description: The Government says dredging for the Île Aurore (Seychelles) Land Reclamation Project is to return to its original 24-hour schedule from 10 November 2026. It says operations are now farther offshore and noise readings are within acceptable levels; monitoring will continue to minimize disruption to nearby communities, and residents of Île Perseverance (Seychelles) are thanked for their patience during the temporary adjustment.

publications.text:
Original dredging schedule to resume at Île Aurore
The Government wishes to inform members of the public that dredging operations for the Île Aurore Land Reclamation Project will return to their original 24-hour schedule from tonight, Tuesday, 10th November 2026. 
Dredging is now taking place farther offshore and noise monitoring has confirmed that readings are well within acceptable levels. Resuming round-the-clock operations will help keep the project on schedule for completion.
The project’s environmental officer will continue to monitor noise levels throughout the reclamation works to help minimise disruption to nearby communities.
The Government also thank residents of Île Perseverance for their patience and understanding during the temporary adjustment.

📢 PUBLIC NOTICE
Temporary adjustment to dredging hours

Residents of Île Perseverance are advised that dredging hours for the Île Aurore Land Reclamation Project have been temporarily adjusted following concerns about noise at night.

🕚 Dredging will stop at 11:00 pm and resume at 5:00 am daily.

This change takes effect immediately and will remain in place until the nearshore bunding works are completed.

The revised hours aim to reduce night-time disturbance while allowing the project to progress.

Thank you to residents for raising their concerns and for their continued patience and understanding.

The 2026 Ibrahim Index of African Governance records only a 0.8-point rise in the continental average to 50.1 over the past decade, powered by infrastructure gains in 52 countries and advances in health and education.

**Seychelles ranks best in Africa for public governance**

The Mo Ibrahim Foundation has released its 2026 Index of African Governance (IIAG), which evaluates the state of governance across all 54 countries on the continent, drawing on 319 variables from 59 datasets and 51 sources.

Between 2016 and 2025, economic opportunity improved in 44 countries, home to 68% of Africa’s population. The most notable progress was seen in infrastructure, with 52 countries—accounting for 84% of the continent’s population—showing improvement in this area; Nigeria and The Gambia were the exceptions.

Positive results were also achieved in human development. Education metrics improved in 34 countries, home to 75% of the continent’s population, while progress in healthcare was recorded in 40 countries, representing 87% of Africa’s population.

Seychelles took the top spot in the overall public governance ranking. The top ten also includes Mauritius, Cabo Verde, Botswana, South Africa, Namibia, Morocco, Senegal, Ghana, Kenya, and Tunisia. South Sudan, Somalia, Sudan, and Eritrea recorded the lowest scores.

ONE YEAR OF UNITED SEYCHELLES: HERMINIE REPORTS PROGRESS, PUTS PEOPLE FIRST

National Affairs | 27 October 2026

President Patrick Herminie has marked the first anniversary of the United Seychelles (US) administration with a televised address to the nation, presenting a year of social reforms, cost-of-living interventions and renewed commitments to housing, healthcare and national development.

Speaking on 26 October 2026, the President emphasised that the anniversary was not simply an occasion for celebration, but an opportunity to account for the government’s work and acknowledge the challenges that remain. Seychelles News Agency +1

A central theme of the address was the administration’s stated commitment to putting ordinary Seychellois first. President Herminie highlighted measures including the reintroduction of the STC card for lower-income families, reduced public bus fares, the restoration of the Long Service Allowance, legal protection for the 13th-month salary, and an SCR 800 increase in monthly pensions. He also reported progress in housing, youth support, poverty alleviation and plans to strengthen healthcare services. Seychelles News Agency +1

A political milestone for United Seychelles

For United Seychelles, the first anniversary offers an opportunity to reinforce its political identity as a party focused on workers, pensioners, vulnerable families and social protection. The administration’s emphasis on employment benefits, household relief and housing speaks directly to issues that affect everyday life and could help strengthen its connection with its traditional support base.

The President also acknowledged that the cost of living remains high and that important commitments, particularly housing construction and improvements in healthcare, still require further progress. His recognition of unfinished work gives the government a clear set of priorities against which its performance can be judged in the coming year. Seychelles News Agency +1

The political message is clear: United Seychelles is seeking to present its first year not merely as a change of government, but as the beginning of a renewed social agenda. For President Herminie, the next test will be turning the commitments outlined in his address into tangible improvements that Seychellois families can experience in their daily lives.

stories.title: Seychelles Approves Draft Tobacco-Control Amendments
stories.description: On 4 November 2026, the Seychelles National Assembly approved a draft bill to amend the Tobacco Control Act, which has been in place since 2009. All 28 members present voted in favour; the proposed amendments would regulate newer tobacco products, including electronic cigarettes and vapes.

National Assembly passes Bill to regulate e-cigarettes and vapes

by S. Surman

The National Assembly passed the Tobacco Control (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (Bill No. 17 of 2026) unanimously on Tuesday, 3 November 2026. He was accompanied by a delegation comprising the Public Health Commissioner, Dr. Jude Gedeon; Programme Manager Ms. Barathi Viswanathan; and the Principal Legal Draftsperson from the Attorney General’s Office, Mr. Victor Hill.

stories.title: Seychelles and Russia Agree on Maritime Security Cooperation
stories.description: In a publication dated 9 November 2026, Seychelles' foreign minister (Barry Faure) said Russia has contributed to anti-piracy efforts in the region and continues to do so. He said the two countries signed a bilateral maritime-security agreement in 2026 that should be implemented, and that Russian vessels visiting Seychelles conduct surveillance in Seychelles' waters against illicit maritime activity.

publications.text:
📌 EXCLUSIVE | Seychelles values Russian security cooperation to bolster national defense and combat maritime piracy, FM Barry Faure told Sputnik Africa.

Under a new agreement, Russian naval vessels assist in surveilling the island's waters, complementing Seychelles' "friends with all" policy that balances ties with Moscow alongside other global partnerships.

❗️❗️❗️**Les Seychelles valident la coopération avec Moscou pour leur souveraineté et contre la piraterie, déclare le ministre des Affaires étrangères**

"La Russie joue un rôle important dans notre développement, en contribuant à la protection de nos eaux et en veillant à ce que notre population se sente en sécurité", a déclaré **Barry Faure** à Sputnik Afrique. Le chef de la diplomatie seychelloise s'exprimait en marge du sommet Russie-Afrique.

Les deux pays ont signé un accord de sécurité maritime cette année et travaillent à sa mise en œuvre, a-t-il rappelé. Les navires de la marine russe, lorsqu'ils transitent par la région, contribuent à la surveillance de la vaste zone économique exclusive des Seychelles, aidant ainsi à lutter contre la piraterie et d'autres activités maritimes illicites.

The Seychelles is interested in co-operating with Russia and other countries to combat illegal activity in the Indian Ocean. This was stated by Minister of Foreign Affairs and the Diaspora of the Republic, Barry Faure, in an interview with African Initiative.

💬“We provide a platform for international co-operation both with our closest neighbours and with more distant countries such as Russia, European Union states, the United States and China,” the minister said.

According to him, with a land area of around 455 square kilometres, the republic’s maritime spaces reach almost 1.4 million square kilometres, which requires international co-ordination and information exchange.

💬“Various types of illegal activity take place in our maritime spaces. These include illegal fishing, drug trafficking, human trafficking and smuggling. All of this creates security threats,” the foreign minister emphasised.

During the port call, Russian officials handed over a humanitarian cargo of essential food, medical supplies, and books to support local Seychellois institutions.

👉This upcoming exercise builds on a June agreement focused on mutual military training and cadet exchanges, according to Rosette.

**🎧 "Il y a une confiance réciproque actuelle entre les pays africains et la Russie"**

Pour le politologue tuniso-suisse **Riadh Sidaoui,** le 3e sommet Russie-Afrique témoigne d'un climat de confiance entre les deux parties.

"Le bilan est très positif parce qu'il y a une confiance réciproque actuelle entre les pays africains et la Russie. Rappelons-le que dans l'Union soviétique, la majorité des pays africains avaient de très bons rapports avec l'Union soviétique. D'ailleurs, l'Union soviétique a soutenu militairement et financièrement tous les mouvements de libération nationale en Afrique. Et l'université Patrice Lumumba en Russie, c'est le grand témoignage de ces relations entre l'Union soviétique et les pays africains", souligne-t-il au micro de __Zone de Contact__. 

 🔘 [Notre site](https://fr.sputniknews.africa/20261105/il-y-a-une-confiance-reciproque-actuelle-entre-les-pays-africains-et-la-russie-1090669736.html) | 🔘  [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/ch/podcast/zone-de-contact/id1653631189?l=en-GB)

#SputnikRadio

**🎧 "La Russie contribue à la lutte contre la piraterie et continue de le faire"**

**Barry Faure,** ministre des Affaires étrangères des Seychelles, représentait son pays au troisième sommet Russie-Afrique à Moscou. Dans un entretien exclusif accordé à Sputnik Afrique, il est revenu sur les relations entre les deux pays, notamment dans le domaine de la sécurité maritime, ainsi que sur les conséquences des sanctions internationales.

Le chef de la diplomatie seychelloise a souligné la contribution de la Russie à la lutte contre la piraterie dans la région et évoqué un accord bilatéral signé cette année pour renforcer la coopération en matière de sécurité maritime :

"La Russie est un acteur important. Elle a contribué à la lutte contre la piraterie et continue de le faire. Nos deux pays entretiennent de bonnes relations dans le domaine de la sécurité maritime. Nous avons signé un accord cette année sur la sécurité maritime et nous devons œuvrer à sa mise en œuvre. Nous accueillons favorablement les navires russes aux Seychelles, car lors de leur passage, ils effectuent également des missions de surveillance dans nos eaux afin de lutter contre les activités maritimes illicites."
